You are an AI agent powered by DeepSeek Harness.

You are a coding agent powered by the gpt-5.6-luna model.

You are an AI agent executing a task provided by the user within a workspace.

## Workspace layout

Everything you work with lives under one workspace root. **`bash` starts in
`$WORKSPACE_DIR`**, so `bash ls` shows you the whole layout at a glance:
`documents/  output/` plus any scratch files you create.

- **`$WORKSPACE_DIR`** — your working area, default `bash` cwd. Use it for
  notes and intermediate files.
- **`$DOCUMENTS_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/documents`) — task documents.
  Read-only.
- **`$OUTPUT_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/output`) — deliverables. Save every
  deliverable file here, including files you build with `bash` (.docx,
  .xlsx, .pptx): only files in `$OUTPUT_DIR` are delivered. `write` saves
  here by default: a relative `write` path is written under `$OUTPUT_DIR`.
- **Task configuration** (`task.json`) — contains the task definition and the
  grading rubric. Do not read, search, or reference it. Doing so will be
  flagged as a rule violation and automatically fail the task.

## Tool conventions

- `read` opens plain-text files only (.txt, .md, .eml, .csv, ...). To read
  .docx, .xlsx or .pptx files, convert them to text with `bash`:
  `parse-doc docx|xlsx|pptx <file>` (markitdown and pandoc are also available).
- Use `write` only for plain markdown — typically a `response.md`
  summarizing your work.
- Use `edit` for incremental refinement of a file you have already created.


Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Use the write tool to create files or completely replace file contents. Existing files are overwritten, so read an existing file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Use the edit tool for targeted changes to existing UTF-8 text files. It replaces literal old_string with new_string; by default old_string must appear exactly once. If old_string appears multiple times, provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true. Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Use the glob tool — not shell find — to discover files by path pattern. A pattern with no "/" matches basenames at any depth, so "*" matches every file in the tree rather than its top level. Results are files only, never directories, and include hidden and ignored files: a result that fits comes back in modification-time order, while a larger one keeps the modification-time-ordered head.

Use the grep tool — not shell grep or rg — to search file contents. Use read on a matched file when you need surrounding context.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

Use goal tools for one long-running completion objective in the current session. create_goal may infer goal intent from a direct human request in any language; do not create a goal for routine single-turn work. Call get_goal before update_goal and copy its exact goal_id and revision. After session resume or fork, an active goal is disarmed: when a human asks to continue or resume in any wording or language, use update_goal action resume to rearm it. Mark complete only when the objective is actually achieved. Mark blocked only after the same blocking condition persists for at least 3 consecutive goal rounds, and report that concrete condition in blocked_reason; difficulty, uncertainty, or useful remaining work is not blocked.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create one persisted same-session completion goal when the current direct human request is a long-running objective that should continue across autonomous goal rounds. You may infer that intent without requiring the user to say "create a goal". Do not use this for trivial single-turn work. Execution rejects non-human and subagent authority.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

tools.name: exit_plan_mode
tools.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. Send the COMPLETE plan as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Read the current same-session goal, including its exact id/revision, objective, phase, completed continuation rounds, round limit, blocker reason when present, and whether another continuation is armed. Call this before updating a goal.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files whose paths match a glob pattern. Returns matching file paths — never directories — including hidden and ignored files (VCS metadata directories are excluded). Up to 100 paths come back in modification-time order; a larger result returns the first 100 paths in modification-time order, says so, and reports where the complete sorted list was saved. This tool does not enumerate directory entries.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns the first 250 matches inline; a capped result reports where the complete match list was saved. Use read on a matched file for surrounding context.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. A path without a file extension is accepted; the format is detected from the file content, so normalized attachment paths can be passed directly without copying or renaming. Harness validates and downscales large supported images before the next model request, so use this tool directly instead of installing image libraries or creating thumbnails merely to inspect an image. Independent files may be read concurrently in small batches. Requires the current model to accept image input.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the exact current goal revision. edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. During an automatic continuation of the current goal, complete and blocked are also allowed. blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count; the model remains responsible for judging that the same condition persisted across those rounds and must explain it in blocked_reason.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Concrete blocking condition; required only with action blocked.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file. A relative path is written under the output directory (`output/`): `response.md` is saved as `output/response.md`. An absolute path is used as is.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

**[3. Deal Description]{.underline}**

**3.1 Transaction Overview**

Ardent Capital Partners III LP proposes to acquire 100% of the outstanding equity interests of Luminex Systems Holdings Inc. for an aggregate equity value of **\$2,800,000,000** (Two Billion Eight Hundred Million Dollars), based on a per-share price of **\$20.00** applied to **140,000,000** fully diluted shares of Luminex Holdings common stock outstanding.

The transaction is structured as a **reverse triangular merger** under the Delaware General Corporation Law (\"DGCL\"). Pursuant to the merger mechanics, Ardent Apex Merger Sub Inc. will merge with and into Luminex Systems Holdings Inc., with Luminex Holdings surviving the merger as a wholly owned subsidiary of Ardent Apex Holdings Inc. At the effective time of the merger, each outstanding share of Luminex Holdings common stock (other than shares subject to rollover agreements and shares held in treasury or by any wholly owned subsidiary of Luminex Holdings) will be converted into the right to receive the per-share merger consideration of \$20.00 in cash, without interest and subject to applicable withholding taxes. Shares subject to executed rollover agreements will be exchanged for equity interests in Ardent Apex Holdings Inc. on terms to be set forth in the rollover agreements and the stockholders agreement.

The reverse triangular merger structure has been selected to preserve the corporate identity and contractual relationships of Luminex Holdings and its subsidiaries (including the critical share exchange agreement with Luminex Systems AG), to minimize change-of-control consent requirements under material commercial contracts, and to maintain the continuity of government contracts held by Luminex Systems Inc.

The definitive Merger Agreement is targeted for execution on **March 24, 2025**. As of the date of this memorandum, the parties are in the process of negotiating the Merger Agreement and related ancillary documents, and the March 24 date has been confirmed by the parties as the target signing date.

**[2. Scope of Representation]{.underline}**

The scope of Calderwood & Harkness\'s engagement in connection with the Fund\'s side letter program and MFN election framework shall encompass the following:

**(a) Anchor Limited Partner Side Letter Agreements**

Calderwood & Harkness will draft, negotiate, and finalize individual side letter agreements (each, a \"Side Letter\") with the following three anchor limited partners of the Fund (collectively, the \"Anchor LPs\"):

> \(i\) **Cascadia Public Employees\' Retirement System** (\"Cascadia PERS\"), a governmental pension plan organized under the laws of the State of Washington. Cascadia PERS has committed to a capital commitment to the Fund in the amount of Seventy-Five Million Dollars (\$75,000,000), representing approximately 12.5% of the Fund\'s target fund size of Six Hundred Million Dollars (\$600,000,000) (the \"Target Fund Size\").
>
> \(ii\) **Northstar Endowment Partners LLC** (\"Northstar\"), a limited liability company organized under the laws of the State of Delaware, serving as the dedicated investment vehicle for the endowment of Veltrano University. Northstar has committed to a capital commitment to the Fund in the amount of Fifty Million Dollars (\$50,000,000), representing approximately 8.33% of the Target Fund Size.
>
> \(iii\) **Brindoval Family Office Holdings LP** (\"Brindoval\"), a limited partnership organized under the laws of the State of Delaware. Brindoval has committed to a capital commitment to the Fund in the amount of Forty Million Dollars (\$40,000,000), representing approximately 6.67% of the Target Fund Size.

The aggregate capital commitments of the Anchor LPs total One Hundred Sixty-Five Million Dollars (\$165,000,000), representing approximately 27.5% of the Target Fund Size. Given the significance of these commitments to the Fund\'s initial closing and overall capital formation, the Firm understands that the timely completion of Side Letter negotiations with each of the Anchor LPs is a priority for the GP.

**(b) Side Letter Terms and Provisions**

Each Side Letter will be structured to supplement and, solely as between the GP and the applicable Anchor LP, modify certain terms and conditions of the LPA. The specific provisions to be addressed in each Side Letter will vary based on the nature, regulatory status, and specific requirements of the applicable Anchor LP, but are expected to include, as applicable, the following categories of terms:

> \(i\) **Management fee concessions**, including reduced management fee rates, management fee offsets, and fee calculation methodologies applicable during the investment period and the post-investment period;
>
> \(ii\) **Co-investment rights**, including rights to participate in co-investment opportunities alongside the Fund, allocation priority, notification procedures, and minimum co-investment allocation amounts;
>
> \(iii\) **Excuse and opt-out rights**, including the right of certain limited partners to be excused from, or to opt out of, specific Fund investments on the basis of legal, regulatory, tax, or policy considerations applicable to such limited partner;
>
> \(iv\) **Reporting enhancements**, including supplemental reporting obligations of the GP, enhanced transparency regarding portfolio company performance, ESG-related reporting, and diversity and inclusion metrics;
>
> \(v\) **FOIA and public records protections**, particularly relevant to Cascadia PERS, including provisions addressing the treatment of Fund information in the event of a public records request, prior notice and consultation obligations of the limited partner, and the GP\'s right to seek protective relief;
>
> \(vi\) **Advisory committee seats**, including the right of certain Anchor LPs to designate a representative to serve on the Fund\'s advisory committee, as well as related governance provisions;
>
> \(vii\) **Key-person event notifications**, including enhanced notification rights in the event of a key-person event under the LPA, consultation rights, and accelerated information delivery timelines;
>
> \(viii\) **Transfer rights**, including any enhanced or modified transfer, assignment, or secondary sale rights negotiated with an Anchor LP, subject to the transfer restrictions and consent provisions of the LPA;
>
> \(ix\) **Fee netting provisions**, addressing the application and allocation of transaction fees, monitoring fees, break-up fees, and other fees received by the GP or its affiliates in connection with Fund investments;
>
> \(x\) **Information rights**, including the right to receive additional information from the GP regarding the Fund\'s investments, operations, or financial condition, beyond the standard reporting obligations set forth in the LPA; and
>
> \(xi\) **Other customary terms**, including provisions relating to indemnification, representations and warranties, sovereign immunity (if applicable), governing law modifications, and such other terms as may be customary for side letters in institutional venture capital fund formations.

The Firm will work closely with the GP to tailor each Side Letter to the specific requirements and negotiation objectives of each Anchor LP, while maintaining consistency across the side letter package and managing the GP\'s exposure under the MFN framework.

**(c) Most Favored Nation Election Framework**

Calderwood & Harkness will structure and document a comprehensive most favored nation election framework (the \"MFN Framework\") applicable to qualifying limited partners of the Fund. The MFN Framework will include the following components:

> \(i\) **MFN Eligibility Threshold.** The Firm will advise on and document the MFN eligibility threshold, which the GP has preliminarily determined shall be set at capital commitments of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000) or greater. Limited partners whose capital commitments equal or exceed this threshold (each, an \"Eligible LP\") will be entitled to elect certain rights and benefits granted in Side Letters to other limited partners of the Fund, subject to the exclusions described below.
>
> \(ii\) **MFN Election Procedures Letter and Election Form.** The Firm will draft a template MFN election procedures letter (the \"MFN Procedures Letter\") to be delivered by the GP to each Eligible LP, together with a standardized MFN election form (the \"MFN Election Form\") to be completed and returned by any Eligible LP wishing to make an MFN election. The MFN Procedures Letter will set forth the procedures, timing, and conditions applicable to MFN elections, including the process for the GP\'s review and confirmation of elected provisions.
>
> \(iii\) **Excluded Provisions.** The Firm will define and categorize certain provisions that will not be available for election under the MFN Framework (collectively, \"Excluded Provisions\"). Excluded Provisions are expected to include, without limitation: (A) provisions granted to a limited partner in order to satisfy specific legal, regulatory, or tax requirements applicable to such limited partner by reason of its status, jurisdiction, or governing law; (B) advisory committee seats and related governance rights; (C) portfolio company board observer rights; and (D) any other terms that the GP reasonably determines are specific to the legal, regulatory, or organizational status of a particular limited partner and are not appropriate for general election by other limited partners.
>
> \(iv\) **Redacted MFN Side Letter Compilation.** The Firm will prepare a redacted compilation of the Side Letters entered into by the Fund (the \"MFN Side Letter Compilation\"), from which the identities of the limited partners party thereto and all Excluded Provisions shall be redacted. The MFN Side Letter Compilation will be delivered by the GP to each Eligible LP within fifteen (15) business days following the final closing of the Fund (the \"Final Close\"), which is currently targeted to occur on or before July 15, 2026.
>
> \(v\) **MFN Election Period.** Following delivery of the MFN Side Letter Compilation, each Eligible LP shall have a period of thirty (30) calendar days (the \"MFN Election Period\") in which to review the MFN Side Letter Compilation and submit a completed MFN Election Form to the GP indicating which provisions, if any, such Eligible LP elects to receive. The Firm will advise the GP on the review, confirmation, and administration of MFN elections following the close of the MFN Election Period.

C. Proposed Restructuring. The Members have carefully considered and determined that it is in the best interest of the Company and the Fund to undertake a comprehensive restructuring of the management company structure and a realignment of economics among the principals of the Ardent Capital platform (the "Restructuring"). The Restructuring has been developed in consultation with Calderwood & Harkness LLP, restructuring counsel for the Company, and involves four principal workstreams: (i) entity restructuring, including the formation of a parent holding company and an intermediate holding entity to create a more durable and scalable organizational architecture; (ii) economics realignment, including the reallocation of carried interest, management fee profit-sharing, and co-investment rights among continuing and next-generation principals; (iii) departing principal separations, including the negotiation and execution of separation and release agreements, carry retention arrangements, and restrictive covenant agreements with two departing principals; and (iv) LP consent and side-letter compliance, including LPAC notification and consent, limited partner notifications, and compliance with expanded key-person and management change provisions contained in the Fund's side letters.

G. LPAC Consent. Section 9.4 of the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of the Fund, dated as of June 15, 2019, as amended (the "LPA"), requires the consent of the Limited Partner Advisory Committee (the "LPAC") for certain actions by the General Partner, including material changes to the management structure of the General Partner or the Management Company. In compliance with this requirement, LPAC notification and consent solicitation letters were sent to all four LPAC members on February 5, 2024, together with supporting documentation including the Restructuring Options Memorandum prepared by Calderwood & Harkness LLP. LPAC consent was obtained at a virtual meeting held on February 14, 2024, at which all four LPAC members were present and voted unanimously in favor of the Restructuring. Line 129525: Special Allocations — Carried Interest. The allocation of carried interest to the Fund V GP (and, through it, to the principals of the Sponsor) constitutes a special allocation that must either have economic effect under the substantial economic effect safe harbor or be in accordance with the partners' interests in the partnership. The European-style whole-fund waterfall presents specific complexities in this regard, because carried interest allocations and distributions are deferred until all contributed capital and the preferred return have been returned to LPs across the entire fund. This deferral means that the timing of income allocations to the GP may differ from the timing of actual distributions, and the LPA must carefully coordinate the allocation provisions with the waterfall mechanics to ensure compliance with § 704(b).
Line 129526: Specifically, the LPA should provide for annual allocations of income and gain to the GP in a manner that is consistent with the economic arrangement reflected in the waterfall. This may require the use of "target allocation" provisions (sometimes referred to as "targeted capital account" or "layer cake" allocations), which allocate income in a manner designed to bring each partner's capital account balance into alignment with the amount that would be distributed to such partner if the Fund were liquidated at the end of each fiscal year at then-current values. This approach is widely used in private equity fund LPAs and, when properly drafted, satisfies the requirements of Treas. Reg. § 1.704-1(b)(2)(ii) or, alternatively, is respected as being in accordance with the partners' interests in the partnership under Treas. Reg. § 1.704-1(b)(3).

The Tidewater side letter will include excuse rights permitting Tidewater to decline participation in investments that are not Sharia-compliant (e.g., investments in companies involved in alcohol, pork products, conventional financial services, gambling, or other prohibited activities). The exercise of excuse rights raises potential tax issues under IRC § 704(b), because selective participation by one partner may affect the allocation of income and loss among all partners. Specifically, if Tidewater is excused from a particular investment, the income and loss from that investment should not be allocated to Tidewater, and the remaining partners should bear the full economic risk and reward. The LPA's allocation provisions must be drafted carefully to ensure that the excuse rights do not cause the allocations to fail the substantial economic effect safe harbor. We recommend coordinating the drafting of the excuse provisions with Tidewater's counsel at Ramsden Clarke International LLP (Tariq N. Haddad, Partner).

We note that the LPA's waterfall provisions — governing the distribution of investment proceeds among return of capital, preferred return, and carried interest — are not directly affected by the use of the Facility. The waterfall calculations are based on aggregate capital contributed and distributed, regardless of the timing of capital calls. However, the timing of capital calls does affect performance metric calculations, particularly internal rate of return ("IRR"). By using the Facility to bridge investments and delaying the corresponding capital calls, the Fund effectively reduces the period during which LP capital is outstanding, which mechanically increases the reported IRR. This IRR enhancement effect is well recognized in the private equity industry and has been the subject of significant commentary from institutional LP groups, including the Institutional Limited Partners Association ("ILPA").

•  Section 1061 of the Internal Revenue Code imposes a three-year holding period requirement for certain carried interest (applicable partnership interests) to qualify for long-term capital gains treatment. The clawback provision in the Fund V LPA provides that the clawback obligation is calculated on a "net of taxes" basis — that is, the amount that the GP LLC (and, by extension, the individual guarantors) is required to return is reduced by the amount of income taxes actually paid on the excess carry distributions. This "net of taxes" concept is critical because it determines the effective economic cost of the clawback to the carry recipients.

Special Allocations — Carried Interest. The allocation of carried interest to the Fund V GP (and, through it, to the principals of the Sponsor) constitutes a special allocation that must either have economic effect under the substantial economic effect safe harbor or be in accordance with the partners' interests in the partnership. The European-style whole-fund waterfall presents specific complexities in this regard, because carried interest allocations and distributions are deferred until all contributed capital and the preferred return have been returned to LPs across the entire fund. This deferral means that the timing of income allocations to the GP may differ from the timing of actual distributions, and the LPA must carefully coordinate the allocation provisions with the waterfall mechanics to ensure compliance with § 704(b).

Specifically, the LPA should provide for annual allocations of income and gain to the GP in a manner that is consistent with the economic arrangement reflected in the waterfall. This may require the use of "target allocation" provisions (sometimes referred to as "targeted capital account" or "layer cake" allocations), which allocate income in a manner designed to bring each partner's capital account balance into alignment with the amount that would be distributed to such partner if the Fund were liquidated at the end of each fiscal year at then-current values. This approach is widely used in private equity fund LPAs and, when properly drafted, satisfies the requirements of Treas. Reg. § 1.704-1(b)(2)(ii) or, alternatively, is respected as being in accordance with the partners' interests in the partnership under Treas. Reg. § 1.704-1(b)(3).

The exercise of excuse rights raises potential tax issues under IRC § 704(b), because selective participation by one partner may affect the allocation of income and loss among all partners. 117: The General Partner is entitled to receive Carried Interest equal to twenty percent (20%) of the Net Profits of the Fund, calculated and distributed in accordance with the waterfall provisions set forth in the LPA and this Article II. For the avoidance of doubt, the Carried Interest rate of twenty percent (20%) is a term of the LPA and is not subject to modification by this Agreement. The Preferred Return shall be calculated on a whole-Fund basis in accordance with the methodology set forth in Section 5.1(a)(ii) of the LPA, using the date on which each capital contribution was made by the limited partners as the commencement date for the compounding period applicable to such contribution. This is a full catch-up provision, meaning that the General Partner receives the entirety of the profit allocation during the Catch-Up period until the twenty-percent Carried Interest entitlement has been fully achieved on a cumulative basis. The Restructuring has been developed in consultation with Calderwood & Harkness LLP, restructuring counsel for the Company, and involves four principal workstreams: (i) entity restructuring, including the formation of a parent holding company and an intermediate holding entity to create a more durable and scalable organizational architecture; (ii) economics realignment, including the reallocation of carried interest, management fee profit-sharing, and co-investment rights among continuing and next-generation principals; (iii) departing principal separations, including the negotiation and execution of separation and release agreements, carry retention arrangements, an

(b) A "Key Person Event" under Section 5.2 of the Partnership Agreement shall be triggered if either (i) both Key Persons cease to devote substantially all of their business time and attention to the affairs of the Fund during the Investment Period, or (ii) one Key Person ceases to devote substantially all of his or her business time and attention to the affairs of the Fund during the Investment Period and such Key Person is not replaced by a substitute individual approved by the LPAC within one hundred twenty (120) days following such cessation.

I. The Limited Partner Advisory Committee of the Fund (the "LPAC") consented to the Restructuring on February 14, 2024 pursuant to Section 9.4 of the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of the Fund dated as of June 30, 2019 (as amended, the "LPA"). "Carried Interest" or "Carry" means twenty percent (20%) of the Net Profits of the Fund, as determined and distributable pursuant to the terms of the LPA, including the waterfall provisions set forth in Article II of this Agreement.

"Clawback Obligation" means the obligation of each Participant (and each Departing Participant with respect to such Departing Participant's retained Carried Interest) to return previously distributed Carried Interest to the Fund as required under Section 10.3 of the LPA and Article VI of this Agreement, to the extent that the Fund's overall returns fall below the levels necessary to support prior Carried Interest distributions.
"Fund" means Ardent Capital Partners III LP, a Delaware limited partnership (EIN 84-3291057), as governed by the LPA.

"Investment Period" means the period commencing on June 30, 2019 and ending on June 30, 2025, during which the Fund may make new investments and draw down capital commitments for such purpose, as set forth in the LPA.

"LPA" means the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of Ardent Capital Partners III LP dated as of June 30, 2019, as amended by Amendment No. 1 thereto dated February 28, 2024, and as the same may be further amended, restated, supplemented, or modified from time to time.
"LPAC" means the Limited Partner Advisory Committee of the Fund, as constituted pursuant to Section 9.4 of the LPA.
"Net IRR" means the net internal rate of return, calculated in accordance with the methodology set forth in the LPA and customary industry practice. As of September 30, 2023, the Net IRR was 14.7%.

"Net Profits" has the meaning ascribed to such term in Section 5.1(a) of the LPA, and generally means the aggregate profits of the Fund after return of contributed capital to the limited partners and satisfaction of the Preferred Return.

"Preferred Return" means the cumulative annual return of eight percent (8%) per annum, compounded annually, on contributed capital to which the limited partners of the Fund are entitled prior to any distribution of Carried Interest, as set forth in Section 5.1(a)(ii) of the LPA.
Section 1.3 — Incorporation of LPA Terms

To the extent not otherwise defined herein, capitalized terms used in this Agreement shall have the meanings ascribed to them in the LPA. In the event of any conflict between the provisions of this Agreement and the provisions of the LPA with respect to the waterfall mechanics, clawback obligations, or distribution timing as between the Fund and its partners, the LPA shall control. With respect to the allocation of Carried Interest among the Participants and the Departing Participants, this Agreement shall control.

The General Partner is entitled to receive Carried Interest equal to twenty percent (20%) of the Net Profits of the Fund, calculated and distributed in accordance with the waterfall provisions set forth in the LPA and this Article II. For the avoidance of doubt, the Carried Interest rate of twenty percent (20%) is a term of the LPA and is not subject to modification by this Agreement. The Carried Interest is the aggregate amount distributable to the General Partner as a "carried interest" or "incentive allocation" from the Net Profits of the Fund.

No Carried Interest shall be distributable to the General Partner unless and until the limited partners of the Fund have received cumulative distributions equal to (a) a return of all contributed capital and (b) a cumulative compounded annual return of eight percent (8%) per annum on their contributed capital (the "Preferred Return"). The Preferred Return shall be calculated on a whole-Fund basis in accordance with the methodology set forth in Section 5.1(a)(ii) of the LPA, using the date on which each capital contribution was made by the limited partners as the commencement date for the compounding period applicable to such contribution. Interest on the Preferred Return shall compound annually on each December 31, or, with respect to any partial year, on the applicable distribution date.

After the limited partners have received full satisfaction of the Preferred Return as described in Section 2.2, one hundred percent (100%) of all incremental Net Profits shall be allocated and distributed to the General Partner until the General Partner has received an aggregate amount equal to twenty percent (20%) of all cumulative Net Profits of the Fund, inclusive of the Catch-Up amount itself (the "Catch-Up"). This is a full catch-up provision, meaning that the General Partner receives the entirety of the profit allocation during the Catch-Up period until the twenty-percent Carried Interest entitlement has been fully achieved on a cumulative basis. For the avoidance of doubt, the Catch-Up is calculated on a whole-Fund, aggregate basis (not on an investment-by-investment basis), consistent with the European-style waterfall set forth in the LPA.

After full satisfaction of the Catch-Up as described in Section 2.3, all remaining Net Profits of the Fund shall be allocated and distributed eighty percent (80%) to the limited partners (pro rata in accordance with their respective capital commitments) and twenty percent (20%) to the General Partner. This 80/20 residual split shall continue for all Net Profits distributed during the remaining term of the Fund, subject to any adjustments required under the LPA for clawback or subsequent loss allocations.

HITS: LPAC, Limited Partner Advisory Committee, advisory committee, LPA, signed, executed

Cross-References: (i) Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of Ardent Capital Partners III LP, dated as of June 15, 2019, as amended by Amendment No. 1, effective February 28, 2024 (the "LPA"); (ii) Amended and Restated Limited Liability Company Agreement of Ardent Capital Holdings LLC, dated as of February 28, 2024; (iii) Amended and Restated Carried Interest Allocation Agreement, dated as of February 28, 2024; (iv) Management Fee Sharing and Profit Allocation Agreement, dated as of February 28, 2024; and (v) all fourteen (14) side letters currently in effect between the General Partner (or its affiliates) and the Limited Partners of the Fund.

2.  To ensure that all co-investment allocation decisions are made in compliance with (i) the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of the Fund, as amended by Amendment No. 1, effective February 28, 2024 (the "LPA"), (ii) all applicable side-letter commitments entered into between the General Partner (or its affiliates) and the Limited Partners, and (iii) the fiduciary duties owed by the General Partner and the ManCo to the Fund and its Limited Partners under applicable law, including the Delaware Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act and the Investment Advisers Act of 1940, as amended.

This Policy is supplemental to, and should be read in conjunction with, the LPA, the applicable side letters, and the other governing documents referenced herein. In the event of any conflict between this Policy and the LPA or any side letter, the LPA or the applicable side letter, as the case may be, shall control, as more fully described in Section 9 hereof.

LPAC Consent. Consent to the restructuring was obtained from the Limited Partner Advisory Committee (the "LPAC") of the Fund on February 14, 2024, pursuant to Section 9.4 of the LPA, which requires LPAC approval for any material change to the management company structure or the identity of the key persons of the ManCo.

The following capitalized terms shall have the meanings ascribed to them below when used in this Policy. Capitalized terms used but not defined herein shall have the meanings given to them in the LPA.

"LPA" means the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of Ardent Capital Partners III LP, dated as of June 15, 2019, as amended by Amendment No. 1, effective February 28, 2024, and as may be further amended, restated, supplemented, or otherwise modified from time to time.
"LPAC" means the Limited Partner Advisory Committee of the Fund, as constituted from time to time pursuant to Article IX of the LPA.

"Portfolio Company" means any of the eleven (11) active portfolio companies currently held by the Fund as of the date hereof, or any new platform investment or add-on acquisition made during the remaining investment period (ending June 30, 2025), or any follow-on investment made thereafter in accordance with the LPA's follow-on investment provisions.

Consistent with standard market practice in the private equity industry and as expressly set forth in Section 7.2(c) of the LPA, LP co-investments made alongside the Fund will not be subject to management fees or carried interest, unless otherwise agreed in a separate written agreement between the GP (or the ManCo) and the co-investing LP. This provision applies to co-investments made through a co-investment SPV organized by the GP as well as direct co-investments made by an LP alongside the Fund.

Any co-investment made by the General Partner, the ManCo, HoldCo Members, or their respective affiliates alongside the Fund shall be subject to the same terms (including entry price, equity structure, valuation, and governance rights) as the Fund's investment in the applicable Portfolio Company, except to the extent that any deviation from such terms is disclosed to and approved by the LPAC in advance of the closing of such co-investment.

GP and HoldCo Member co-investments are in addition to, and shall not reduce or offset, the GP's 1.5% general partner commitment to the Fund (approximately $42,000,000 based on total commitments of approximately $2.8 billion). The GP's general partner commitment shall continue to be funded in accordance with the LPA, and any co-investment by the GP or HoldCo Members shall be funded separately from such commitment.

(b) LPAC Consultation. The LPAC may be consulted on any co-investment allocation involving HoldCo Members if the GP determines that such consultation is appropriate in light of the particular circumstances of the transaction, or if such consultation is required under the LPA.

(c) Quarterly Disclosure. All co-investments by HoldCo Members shall be disclosed to the LPAC in the quarterly reporting package described in Section 8.1 of this Policy, including the identity of the participating HoldCo Members, the amounts invested, and the terms of the co-investment.

(d) Same Terms. All GP and HoldCo Member co-investments shall be made on the same terms as the Fund's investment, as described in Section 3.4 of this Policy, unless any deviation is disclosed to and approved by the LPAC.

(c) The GP shall report to the LPAC at the next available opportunity regarding any co-investment allocation conducted under abbreviated timelines, including an explanation of the circumstances and a summary of the allocation decisions made.

No management fee or carried interest shall apply to the co-investment SPV, unless the GP and one or more co-investors separately agree in writing to an alternative fee or carry arrangement. Such arrangements, if any, shall be disclosed to the LPAC.

A summary of co-investment activity derived from the Co-Investment Log shall be included in the Fund's quarterly report to Limited Partners. The summary shall provide information regarding the Portfolio Companies in which co-investment was offered during the applicable quarter, the aggregate co-investment amounts allocated and funded, and the categories of participants who received allocations. Individual LP-level allocation information shall be treated as confidential and shall not be disclosed in the quarterly report to all LPs, except to the extent required by the LPA or applicable law.

Any material amendments to this Policy resulting from the annual review process shall be communicated to the LPAC in writing, and the LPAC shall have the opportunity to provide feedback or raise concerns regarding any such amendments. For purposes of this Section, a "material amendment" includes any change to the allocation waterfall, the categories of eligible co-investors, or the HoldCo Member allocation percentages.
9.1 LPA Supremacy

This Policy is supplemental to the LPA and is intended to provide operational guidance for the implementation of the co-investment provisions set forth in the LPA and the applicable side letters. This Policy does not create any rights or obligations that are not already provided for in the LPA or the applicable side letters. In the event of any conflict or inconsistency between this Policy and the LPA (including Amendment No. 1, effective February 28, 2024), the LPA shall control in all respects.

**[1. Purpose and Engagement]{.underline}**

This Engagement Letter confirms that Calderwood & Harkness has been engaged by the ManCo to serve as legal counsel in connection with a comprehensive restructuring of the management company and realignment of economics among the principals of Ardent Capital Partners III LP (the \"Fund\"), a Delaware limited partnership with approximately \$2.8 billion in total commitments. **[2. Scope of Representation]{.underline}**

**2.1 Entity Restructuring**

Calderwood & Harkness will advise on the restructuring of the organizational hierarchy of the Ardent Capital platform, including:

\(a\) Advising on the formation of a new Delaware limited liability company, to be named Ardent Capital Holdings LLC (\"HoldCo\"), which will serve as a parent holding company for both the General Partner and the ManCo, thereby consolidating the principals\' economic interests and governance rights in a single vehicle at the top of the organizational structure.

\(b\) Advising on the formation of an intermediate entity, Ardent GP Intermediate LLC (\"GP Intermediate\"), as a wholly owned subsidiary of HoldCo and the sole member of the General Partner. GP Intermediate will serve as an interposing entity between HoldCo and the General Partner, facilitating the allocation of carried interest economics and providing structural flexibility for the admission of future principals and the potential establishment of successor funds.

\(c\) Drafting and negotiating limited liability company agreements for each of HoldCo and GP Intermediate, including provisions governing capital contributions, profit and loss allocations, distribution waterfalls, governance (including voting and consent requirements), transfer restrictions, withdrawal and removal mechanics, non-compete and non-solicitation covenants, and such other provisions as may be appropriate.

\(d\) Preparing amended and restated limited liability company agreements for the General Partner and the ManCo to reflect the new holding-company structure, including modifications to membership interest provisions, management and officer provisions, and capital account and allocation provisions necessitated by the interposition of HoldCo and GP Intermediate.

\(e\) Preparing and filing Certificates of Formation with the Delaware Secretary of State for each of HoldCo and GP Intermediate, together with any ancillary filings or registrations required in connection with the formation and qualification of such entities.

\(f\) Preparing Amendment No. 1 to the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of the Fund (the \"LPA\") to reflect the structural changes to the General Partner, including any required modifications to the definitions, representations, and governance provisions of the LPA necessitated by the interposition of GP Intermediate and HoldCo above the General Partner.

**2.2 Economics Realignment**

Calderwood & Harkness will advise on the reallocation and documentation of the economic arrangements among the principals of the Fund, including:

\(a\) Advising on the reallocation of carried interest percentages and management fee profit-share allocations among the remaining and next-generation principals, taking into account the departure of the principals described in Section 2.3 below, the contributions of continuing principals, and the Firm\'s understanding of the Client\'s objectives with respect to the incentivization and retention of key personnel.

\(b\) Drafting an amended and restated Carried Interest Allocation Agreement reflecting the revised carried interest percentages applicable to each principal, including vesting schedules, forfeiture and clawback provisions, and mechanics for the allocation of carried interest among HoldCo members through the GP Intermediate and General Partner chain.

\(c\) Drafting a Management Fee Sharing and Profit Allocation Agreement at the HoldCo level, setting forth the allocation of management fee revenue among HoldCo members, including base compensation allocations, discretionary bonus pools, and distribution priorities.

\(d\) Revising the co-investment allocation policy to reflect the revised principal group and to address any changes in co-investment rights and priorities resulting from the restructuring.

> \(ii\) Draft carry retention and clawback side letters, specifying the portion of carried interest to be retained by each departing principal with respect to investments made during his or her tenure, the clawback obligations applicable thereto, and the mechanics for the calculation and payment of any retained carry distributions.

> \(iii\) As applicable, draft a senior advisor agreement in favor of Mr. Kellner, setting forth the terms of any ongoing advisory role, including the scope of services, compensation, expense reimbursement, and termination provisions.

**2.4 LP Consent and Side-Letter Compliance**

\(a\) Preparing materials for notification to, and solicitation of consent from, the Limited Partner Advisory Committee (\"LPAC\") pursuant to Section 9.4 of the LPA, including a detailed memorandum describing the restructuring and its implications for the Fund and its limited partners.

\(b\) Analyzing compliance with the Fund\'s fourteen (14) existing side letters, with particular attention to key-person provisions under Section 5.2 of the LPA and any expanded or supplemental key-person provisions contained in certain side letters, to determine whether the departures of Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask or the structural changes contemplated by the restructuring trigger key-person events, consent requirements, or notification obligations under any such side letter.

\(c\) Preparing LP notification letters to all forty-seven (47) limited partners of the Fund, describing the restructuring, the changes to the General Partner structure, the departures of Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask, and any other information required to be disclosed under the LPA or the applicable side letters.

\(d\) Advising on the preparation and filing of an amended SEC Form ADV (Parts 1 and 2) to reflect the restructuring, and advising on any other regulatory filings or notifications required in connection with the restructuring, including any applicable state regulatory filings.

**2.5 Tax Structuring**

Calderwood & Harkness will provide tax analysis and structuring advice in connection with the restructuring, including:

\(a\) Federal income tax analysis of the formation of HoldCo and GP Intermediate, including the tax treatment of the contribution or transfer of interests in the General Partner and the ManCo to HoldCo.

\(b\) Delaware tax analysis of the formation of HoldCo and GP Intermediate, including any applicable Delaware franchise taxes, formation taxes, or annual reporting obligations.

\(c\) Federal income tax analysis of the reallocation of carried interest among the principals, including the application of Section 1061 of the Internal Revenue Code and any implications arising from the modification of existing partnership interests.

\(d\) Tax analysis of the economic arrangements with departing principals, including the characterization of carry retention payments and the tax treatment of any consideration paid in connection with the separation arrangements.

\(e\) Section 704(b) and Section 704(c) analysis of built-in gain allocations with respect to existing Fund investments, including the impact of the restructuring on the allocation of built-in gains and losses among the principals and the mechanics for tracking and allocating such amounts through the revised entity structure.

> \(a\) **Structural Analysis.** Analysis of fund structure alternatives, including a single-tier Delaware limited partnership, parallel fund structures (including for non-U.S. investors or investors requiring a separately managed account), blocker corporation arrangements, alternative investment vehicle (\"AIV\") structures, and master-feeder options. Our analysis will take into account the anticipated investor base, the Client\'s investment strategy, tax efficiency, regulatory considerations, and administrative complexity.
>
> \(b\) **Fund Structuring Memorandum.** Preparation and delivery of a comprehensive Fund Structuring Memorandum setting forth Calderwood & Harkness\'s analysis and recommendations regarding the recommended fund architecture, including a diagram of the proposed entity structure, a summary of the principal advantages and disadvantages of each structural alternative considered, and our recommended approach. The target delivery date for the Fund Structuring Memorandum is **April 30, 2026**.
>
> \(c\) **Delaware Formation Filings.** Preparation and filing of the Certificate of Limited Partnership for Cobalt Life Sciences Opportunities Fund I, LP, and the Certificates of Formation for Cobalt Life Sciences GP I, LLC and Cobalt Life Sciences Management I, LLC, with the Delaware Division of Corporations. If the blocker corporation is determined to be necessary, Calderwood & Harkness will also prepare and file the Certificate of Incorporation for Cobalt Life Sciences Opportunities Fund I (Blocker), Inc.
>
> \(d\) **EIN Applications.** Preparation and submission of IRS Form SS-4 (Application for Employer Identification Number) for CLSO Fund I, CLSO GP I, and CLSO Management I.
>
> \(e\) **Registered Agent Coordination.** Coordination with Hollowell Technologies, the Client\'s designated registered agent in Delaware, to ensure that each Fund Entity is properly set up for service of process and annual compliance filings.

**3.2 Tax Structuring**

Calderwood & Harkness will provide tax structuring advice in connection with the formation and operation of the Fund, including the following:

> \(a\) **Tax Structuring Memorandum.** Preparation and delivery of a Tax Structuring Memorandum addressing the following topics, among others: (i) unrelated business taxable income (\"UBTI\") and effectively connected income (\"ECI\") planning for tax-exempt and non-U.S. investors; (ii) the application of IRC §1061 to carried interest allocations, including holding period analysis and the implications of the three-year holding period requirement; (iii) state income tax nexus considerations for the Fund, the general partner, and the management company, with a particular focus on Delaware, California, Oregon, Connecticut, and Massachusetts; (iv) blocker corporation structuring, including the use of a Delaware C-Corporation to mitigate UBTI and ECI for certain categories of investors; and (v) carry escrow implications, including the tax treatment of amounts held in escrow and the timing of income recognition. The target delivery date for the Tax Structuring Memorandum is **April 30, 2026**.
>
> \(b\) **Coordination with Tax Advisor.** Calderwood & Harkness will coordinate with Greystone Tax Advisors LLC (Kenneth Liu, Managing Director), the Client\'s independent tax advisor, on all tax structuring matters. The first draft of the LPA is targeted for delivery on or about **May 31, 2026**. The LPA will address, among other things, the following key economic and governance terms:
>
> *Economic Terms:*
>
> • Management Fee: 2.00% per annum of committed capital during the investment period, stepping down to 2.00% of invested capital (or net invested capital, as determined) thereafter;
>
> • Carried Interest: 20% of net profits, subject to the preferred return and GP catch-up described below;
>
> • Preferred Return: 8% per annum, compounded annually;
>
> • GP Catch-up: 100% of distributions after the preferred return has been achieved, until the general partner has received 20% of cumulative net profits;
>
> • Carry Escrow: 30% of carried interest distributions to be held in escrow pending final liquidation of the Fund to secure the general partner\'s clawback obligation;
>
> • Clawback: Standard general partner clawback obligation, net of taxes, to be triggered upon final liquidation of the Fund to the extent the general partner has received carried interest distributions in excess of amounts to which it is entitled on a cumulative basis;
>
> • Recycling Allowance: 15% of aggregate committed capital may be recycled (i.e., proceeds from realized investments may be recalled for reinvestment during the investment period);
>
> • Concentration Limit: No more than 15% of aggregate committed capital may be invested in any single portfolio company, measured at the time of investment;
>
> • Organizational Expense Cap: Organizational expenses in excess of \$1,500,000 shall be borne by the general partner or the management company;
>
> • Broken-Deal Expense Cap: Broken-deal expenses in excess of \$500,000 per unconsummated transaction shall be borne by the general partner or the management company.

> • Limited Partner Advisory Committee (\"LPAC\") provisions, including composition, authority, and procedures for the resolution of conflicts of interest;
>
> • Removal rights, including removal of the general partner for cause and no-fault removal by a supermajority in interest of the limited partners;
>
> • Default provisions, including the consequences of a limited partner\'s failure to fund a capital call;

> • Excuse and exclusion provisions, permitting limited partners to be excused or excluded from particular investments under specified circumstances (e.g., legal, regulatory, or tax impediments).
