Dear Ms. Sato:

**[1. Introduction and Engagement Overview]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"C&H\" or the \"Firm\") is pleased to confirm its engagement by Driftwood Capital Management LLC (\"DCM\"), a Delaware limited liability company (EIN: 82-4917653), in its capacity as the General Partner of Driftwood Absolute Return Fund Ltd. (\"DARF\" or the \"Fund\"), a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership registered with the Cayman Islands Registrar of Exempted Limited Partnerships under Registration No. ELP-87234. This engagement letter sets forth the terms and conditions under which C&H will provide legal advisory services to DCM and the Fund in connection with the Key Person Event (as defined below) and related governance matters described herein.

The Fund is governed by its Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement dated March 15, 2017 (as amended from time to time, the \"A&R LPA\"), which is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware. The A&R LPA provides for certain key-person protections in favor of the Fund\'s limited partners, as more fully described in Section 3 below.

This engagement is precipitated by the medical incapacitation of Marcus J. Whitmore, Founder, Chief Investment Officer, and Managing Member (holding a ninety percent (90%) membership interest) of DCM. Mr. Whitmore suffered a severe hemorrhagic stroke on June 3, 2024, and has been incapacitated since that date. Mr. Whitmore is the sole individual designated as a \"Key Person\" under Section 8.04(a) of the A&R LPA. As a result of Mr. Whitmore\'s continued incapacitation for a period exceeding seven consecutive calendar days from the date of the medical event, a Key Person Event under Section 8.04(b) of the A&R LPA is deemed to have been triggered as of June 10, 2024 (the \"Key Person Event\"). The occurrence of the Key Person Event gives rise to a number of contractual obligations, rights, and remedies under the A&R LPA that require prompt legal attention and careful navigation by DCM in its capacity as General Partner of the Fund.

This engagement letter confirms the terms and conditions under which C&H will provide legal advisory services to the Clients (as defined below) in connection with the Key Person Event, including, without limitation, analysis of the A&R LPA\'s key-person provisions, preparation of required limited partner notifications, development of a successor governance framework, drafting of LPA amendments, and coordination of the limited partner consent solicitation process.

**[2. Clients]{.underline}**

For purposes of this engagement, C&H\'s clients shall consist of both DCM and DARF (collectively, the \"Clients\").

DCM\'s principal office is located at 680 Lexington Avenue, 31st Floor, New York, NY 10022. DCM\'s registered agent for service of process in the State of Delaware is Capitol Registered Agents, Inc., located at 1209 Orange Street, Wilmington, Delaware 19801.

DARF\'s registered office is located at 4th Floor, Harbour Place, 103 South Church Street, George Town, Grand Cayman, KY1-1104, Cayman Islands. DARF\'s registered agent in the Cayman Islands is Archipelago Corporate Services Ltd., P.O. Box 2681, George Town, Grand Cayman, KY1-1111, Cayman Islands.

It is important that the scope of this representation be clearly understood. C&H represents DCM and DARF as described herein and does not represent any individual limited partner of the Fund, the Investor Advisory Committee of the Fund (the \"IAC\"), or any individual member or officer of DCM in his or her personal capacity. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, C&H does not represent Mr. Whitmore individually, nor does C&H represent any member of the IAC in his, her, or its individual or fiduciary capacity. Each such person and entity is encouraged to seek independent legal counsel to the extent such person or entity deems it necessary or appropriate.

Elaine R. Sato, in her capacity as Deputy Chief Investment Officer and Managing Member (holding a ten percent (10%) membership interest) of DCM, will serve as the primary point of contact for the Clients in connection with this engagement. All communications from C&H regarding this engagement will be directed to Ms. Sato unless otherwise instructed in writing by Ms. Sato. C&H will take direction from Ms. Sato with respect to all matters within the scope of this engagement, subject to the Firm\'s professional obligations.

**[3. Scope of Representation]{.underline}**

C&H\'s representation of the Clients will encompass the following workstreams in connection with the Key Person Event triggered under Section 8.04 of the A&R LPA. Each workstream is described in further detail below.

**3.1 Key-Person Event Analysis**

C&H will undertake a comprehensive analysis of the mechanics and consequences of Section 8.04 of the A&R LPA, including the following:

> \(a\) **Section 8.04(a) --- Definition of \"Key Person.\"** C&H will confirm the scope of the \"Key Person\" designation under the A&R LPA, which identifies Marcus J. Whitmore as the sole designated Key Person. C&H will analyze the definition for purposes of establishing the factual predicate for the Key Person Event and for advising on the requirements for designating any Successor Key Person(s) (as described in Section 3.3 below).
>
> \(b\) **Section 8.04(b) --- Trigger Conditions.** C&H will analyze the trigger conditions set forth in Section 8.04(b) of the A&R LPA in light of the facts surrounding Mr. Whitmore\'s incapacitation. Specifically, Section 8.04(b) provides that a Key Person Event is deemed to occur when the Key Person becomes unable, whether by reason of death, disability, incapacity, departure, or otherwise, to devote substantially all of his professional time and attention to the affairs of the Fund for a period of seven (7) consecutive calendar days. Based on the information provided to C&H, Mr. Whitmore has been continuously incapacitated since June 3, 2024, and the seven-consecutive-calendar-day threshold was met as of June 10, 2024. C&H will prepare a memorandum confirming the legal basis for this determination.
>
> \(c\) **Section 8.04(c) --- Consequences of the Key Person Event.** C&H will advise the Clients regarding the full range of consequences triggered by the occurrence of the Key Person Event under Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA, which include the following:
>
> \(i\) *Immediate Suspension of the Investment Period.* The Investment Period (as defined in Section 1.01 of the A&R LPA) is automatically suspended upon the occurrence of a Key Person Event. During such suspension, the General Partner may not make new portfolio investments on behalf of the Fund, except as provided in clause (ii) below.
>
> \(ii\) *Follow-On Investment Cap.* Notwithstanding the suspension of the Investment Period, the General Partner retains limited authority to make follow-on investments in existing portfolio positions in an aggregate amount not to exceed one percent (1%) of the Fund\'s assets under management as of the date of the Key Person Event. Based on the Fund\'s most recently reported AUM of approximately \$2.87 billion, the follow-on investment cap is \$28.7 million.
>
> \(iii\) *LP Notification Requirement.* The General Partner is required to provide written notice to all limited partners of the occurrence of the Key Person Event within five (5) business days of the date on which the Key Person Event is deemed to have occurred. Given that the Key Person Event is deemed to have occurred on June 10, 2024, the contractual deadline for delivery of such notice is June 17, 2024.
>
> \(iv\) *Commencement of the 90-Calendar-Day Cure Period.* Upon the occurrence of the Key Person Event, a cure period of ninety (90) calendar days (the \"Cure Period\") commences, during which the General Partner may propose one or more Successor Key Persons for approval by the limited partners. The Cure Period with respect to the current Key Person Event will expire on September 8, 2024.
>
> \(v\) *LP Consent Threshold.* Approval of any proposed Successor Key Person(s) requires the affirmative written consent of limited partners holding at least sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66⅔%) of the aggregate capital commitments of all limited partners of the Fund, excluding for this purpose any co-investment by the General Partner. C&H will advise on the calculation of this threshold based on the most current LP commitment schedule maintained by the Fund\'s administrator.
>
> \(d\) **Consequences of Failure to Cure.** C&H will further analyze the consequences under Section 8.04(d) of the A&R LPA if no cure is achieved within the Cure Period, including the limited partners\' right to elect, by the same 66⅔% consent threshold described above, either (x) to extend the Cure Period for one or more additional periods or (y) to direct the General Partner to commence an orderly wind-down of the Fund\'s portfolio. C&H will advise the Clients on the mechanics, timing, and fiduciary considerations associated with each of these alternatives.
>
> \(e\) **Delaware Law Fiduciary Duty Analysis.** C&H will advise the Clients regarding the fiduciary duties owed by DCM, as General Partner, to the limited partners of the Fund during the Key Person Event and throughout the consent solicitation process, as a matter of Delaware law. This analysis will address, among other things, the duty of care and the contractual modification of fiduciary duties under the A&R LPA, including the exculpation and indemnification provisions set forth in Article XII thereof.

**3.2 LP Notification**

C&H will draft the formal written notice to all forty-seven (47) limited partners of the Fund disclosing the occurrence of the Key Person Event in compliance with Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA (the \"Key Person Notice\"). The Key Person Notice will describe the factual basis for the Key Person Event, the contractual consequences thereof, the commencement and expected expiration date of the Cure Period, and the process by which the General Partner intends to propose Successor Key Person(s) for approval by the limited partners.

C&H will coordinate with Pinnacle Fund Services (Cayman) Ltd. (the \"Administrator\"), the Fund\'s third-party administrator, regarding the maintenance and accuracy of LP contact information, the appropriate method of delivery (including any notice provisions specified in the A&R LPA or in individual side letters), and the mechanics of distributing the Key Person Notice to all limited partners within the contractual timeframe. C&H will confirm with the Administrator that notice is delivered by a method that satisfies the delivery requirements of Section 15.01 of the A&R LPA.

It is critical that the Key Person Notice be delivered within the five (5) business-day contractual notification deadline, which, as noted above, falls on June 17, 2024. C&H will prioritize this workstream accordingly and will endeavor to deliver a draft of the Key Person Notice to Ms. Sato for review no later than June 13, 2024.

**3.3 Successor Governance Framework**

C&H will advise the Clients regarding the identification and evaluation of proposed Successor Key Person(s) and the development of a recommended successor governance framework for the Fund. This advisory work may encompass the following elements:

> \(a\) **Designation of Successor Key Person(s).** C&H will advise on the criteria and process for designating one or more Successor Key Persons under the A&R LPA, including the qualifications, investment experience, and operational capabilities that limited partners are likely to consider in evaluating any proposed successor. C&H will assist in preparing biographical and professional materials for inclusion in the consent solicitation package.
>
> \(b\) **Establishment of an Investment Committee.** In the event that the Clients determine that the successor governance framework should include the establishment of a formal Investment Committee or similar collective governance body (in lieu of, or in addition to, a sole Key Person designation), C&H will advise on the structure, composition, authority, and operating procedures of such body, and will prepare the necessary amendments to the A&R LPA to implement such structure.
>
> \(c\) **Modifications to Key-Person Clause Mechanics.** C&H will advise on potential modifications to the key-person provisions of Section 8.04 of the A&R LPA, which may include revised replacement periods, modified trigger events (including, for example, a threshold requiring the departure or incapacitation of more than one designated Key Person before a Key Person Event is deemed to occur), and other structural changes to reduce single-person dependency risk.
>
> \(d\) **Carried Interest Reallocation.** C&H will advise the Clients on the legal and governance considerations associated with any proposed reallocation of carried interest among GP personnel in connection with the transition, including the interplay between the carried interest provisions of the A&R LPA and the operating agreement of DCM.
>
> \(e\) **Designation of Senior Advisor or Emeritus Role.** To the extent the Clients determine it appropriate, C&H will advise on the creation of a Senior Advisor or emeritus role for Mr. Whitmore, including the scope of any continuing economic interest, advisory responsibilities, and governance rights that may be associated with such role.
>
> \(f\) **Fiduciary Duty Obligations.** Throughout the development of the successor governance framework, C&H will advise the Clients regarding their fiduciary duty obligations under applicable Delaware law, including the duty to act in good faith and in the best interests of the limited partners in proposing any successor governance arrangements.

**3.4 LPA Amendment Drafting**

C&H will prepare one or more amendments to the A&R LPA (each, an \"LPA Amendment\") to implement the successor governance framework developed pursuant to Section 3.3 above. It is anticipated that the LPA Amendments will include modifications to the following provisions of the A&R LPA, among others:

> \(a\) Section 8.04 (Key Person), to reflect the designation of Successor Key Person(s) and any revised key-person clause mechanics;
>
> \(b\) Section 9.02 (Investor Advisory Committee), to the extent any changes to the composition, authority, or procedures of the IAC are contemplated in connection with the successor governance framework;
>
> \(c\) Section 14.01 (Amendments), to the extent any changes to the amendment mechanics are necessary or advisable; and
>
> \(d\) Related schedules and exhibits, including the schedule of Key Persons attached to the A&R LPA.

All LPA Amendments will be subject to the consent requirements set forth in Section 14.01 of the A&R LPA, which generally requires the written consent of the General Partner and limited partners holding at least 66⅔% of aggregate LP capital commitments (excluding GP co-investment) for amendments to certain specified provisions, including Section 8.04. C&H will advise the Clients regarding the applicable consent thresholds for each proposed amendment.

**3.5 LP Consent Solicitation**

C&H will advise on and coordinate the consent solicitation process necessary to obtain limited partner approval of the proposed Successor Key Person(s) and the related LPA Amendments. This workstream will include the following:

> \(a\) **Successor Key Person Proposal Letter.** C&H will draft a detailed letter to all limited partners setting forth the proposed Successor Key Person(s), the rationale for the proposed designation(s), the terms of the proposed successor governance framework, and a summary of the proposed LPA Amendments (the \"Proposal Letter\"). The Proposal Letter will be designed to provide limited partners with all information reasonably necessary to make an informed decision regarding the proposed successor arrangements.
>
> \(b\) **Form of LP Written Consent.** C&H will prepare a Form of LP Written Consent (the \"Consent Form\") for execution by limited partners approving the proposed Successor Key Person(s) and the related LPA Amendments. The Consent Form will be structured to comply with the requirements of Section 14.01 and Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA.
>
> \(c\) **Coordination of Consent Solicitation Process.** C&H will coordinate the distribution of the Proposal Letter and Consent Form to all forty-seven (47) limited partners, working in conjunction with the Administrator to ensure accurate and timely delivery. C&H will manage the consent solicitation timeline with a view toward obtaining the requisite LP consents prior to the expiration of the Cure Period on September 8, 2024.
>
> \(d\) **Tabulation and Certification.** C&H will tabulate the LP consents received and prepare a closing certificate confirming that the requisite consent threshold (66⅔% of aggregate LP capital commitments, excluding GP co-investment) has been satisfied and that the LPA Amendments are effective as of the date specified therein (the \"Closing Certificate\").
>
> \(e\) **Engagement with IAC Counsel.** C&H will engage with counsel to the Investor Advisory Committee, Wexford Crane & Albright LLP, as necessary and appropriate regarding the IAC\'s review of and comments on the proposed Successor Key Person(s), the successor governance framework, and the LPA Amendments. C&H will coordinate with the Clients regarding any modifications to the proposed arrangements that may be requested by the IAC or its counsel.

**[4. Limitations on Scope]{.underline}**

The Clients should be aware of the following limitations on the scope of C&H\'s engagement:

> \(a\) **Cayman Islands Law.** C&H does not provide legal advice regarding the laws of the Cayman Islands. The Clients should consult separately with qualified Cayman Islands counsel regarding any Cayman Islands regulatory, partnership law, or other legal matters that may arise in connection with the Key Person Event or the transactions contemplated by this engagement, including any filings or notifications required under Cayman Islands law in connection with changes to the Fund\'s governance structure.
>
> \(b\) **Tax Advice.** C&H is not engaged to provide tax advice in connection with this engagement. The Clients should consult their own tax advisors regarding the U.S. federal, state, local, and non-U.S. tax implications of any carried interest reallocation, structural changes to the Fund or DCM, or other transactions contemplated by this engagement.
>
> \(c\) **Investment Advice.** C&H is not engaged to provide investment advice or to evaluate the investment merits of any portfolio positions held by the Fund. The Clients acknowledge that any decisions regarding the management, disposition, or retention of portfolio positions during the suspension of the Investment Period or otherwise are solely the responsibility of the Clients and their investment professionals.
>
> \(d\) **Third-Party Service Providers.** C&H does not represent the Fund\'s independent auditor (Graystone & Whitfield LLP), the Fund\'s prime broker (Halcyon Securities International Ltd.), the Administrator, or any other third-party service provider to the Fund or DCM. Each such service provider is represented by its own counsel, and the Clients should not assume that C&H\'s representation extends to any of those parties.
>
> \(e\) **Litigation and Regulatory Matters.** This engagement does not extend to any litigation, arbitration, regulatory investigation, enforcement action, or other adversarial or contested proceeding, whether existing or threatened, unless separately agreed in writing between C&H and the Clients. In the event any such matter arises during the course of this engagement, C&H will promptly advise the Clients and, if requested, discuss the terms of a separate engagement to address such matter.

**[5. Engagement Team]{.underline}**

C&H has assigned the following professionals to this engagement:

  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Name**                **Role**                **Title**
  ----------------------- ----------------------- -------------------------------------
  Graham Sutherland       Responsible Partner     Partner, Funds & Asset Management

  Pamela Cross            Billing Partner         Partner, Funds & Asset Management

  Stephen Adler           Lead Associate          Associate, Funds & Asset Management

  Theresa Kim             Working Associate       Associate, Funds & Asset Management
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Graham Sutherland will serve as the responsible partner overseeing all legal advice rendered in connection with this engagement. Mr. Sutherland will be the Clients\' primary legal point of contact for substantive matters, and all material legal memoranda, draft documents, and advice letters will be reviewed and approved by Mr. Sutherland prior to delivery to the Clients.

Pamela Cross will serve as the billing partner responsible for fee arrangements, invoicing, and all financial aspects of the engagement. Any questions regarding billing, fees, or disbursements should be directed to Ms. Cross.

Stephen Adler will serve as the lead associate responsible for the day-to-day execution of the engagement workstreams described in Section 3 above, under the supervision of Mr. Sutherland. Theresa Kim will support Mr. Adler on all workstreams, with particular focus on document drafting and consent solicitation logistics.

C&H may assign additional attorneys, paralegals, or other professionals to this engagement as reasonably necessary to ensure the timely and effective completion of the workstreams described herein. C&H will provide prior notice to Ms. Sato before assigning any additional professionals whose time will be billed to the Clients.

**[6. Fee Arrangement]{.underline}**

**6.1 Hourly Rates**

Services rendered by C&H attorneys in connection with this engagement will be billed on an hourly basis at the following standard rates:

> • **Partners:** \$1,650 per hour
>
> • **Associates:** \$895 per hour

The foregoing rates are effective as of the date of this engagement letter and are subject to annual adjustment in accordance with C&H\'s standard rate-setting process. C&H will provide the Clients with at least thirty (30) days\' prior written notice of any rate increase. Paralegal and other support staff time, if any, will be billed at rates communicated to the Clients in advance.

**6.2 Fee Cap**

Total professional fees for the engagement shall not exceed Three Hundred Eighty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$385,000) (the \"Fee Cap\") without the prior written consent of the Clients. The Fee Cap encompasses all professional fees of C&H attorneys assigned to this engagement for the workstreams described in Section 3 above. In the event C&H anticipates that total fees may approach or exceed the Fee Cap, C&H will promptly notify the Clients and discuss whether an adjustment to the Fee Cap is warranted. No fees in excess of the Fee Cap will be billed to the Clients absent prior written authorization from Ms. Sato or another authorized representative of DCM. The Fee Cap does not include out-of-pocket disbursements, which are addressed separately in Section 6.3 below.

**6.3 Disbursements and Expenses**

The Clients will reimburse C&H for reasonable out-of-pocket disbursements incurred in connection with this engagement, including, without limitation, costs of document production, photocopying, overnight courier and delivery charges, filing fees, database and research charges, and travel expenses (including airfare, lodging, and ground transportation), if any. All disbursements will be billed at cost, without markup. Disbursements are not subject to the Fee Cap set forth in Section 6.2. C&H will exercise reasonable judgment in incurring disbursements and will obtain the Clients\' prior approval before incurring any single disbursement in excess of Five Thousand Dollars (\$5,000).

**6.4 Billing and Payment**

C&H will issue monthly invoices to DCM at the address set forth in Section 2 above (or to such other address as DCM may designate in writing). Each invoice will include a reasonably detailed description of the services rendered and disbursements incurred during the applicable billing period. Invoices are payable within thirty (30) days of receipt. C&H reserves the right to suspend the performance of services in the event of non-payment of any invoice for a period exceeding sixty (60) days following the date of such invoice, provided that C&H shall provide at least ten (10) days\' prior written notice to the Clients before exercising such right.

**[7. Governing Law]{.underline}**

This engagement letter and the terms and conditions set forth herein shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflicts of law principles that would result in the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction.

For the avoidance of doubt, the A&R LPA is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, and C&H\'s analysis and advice rendered under this engagement with respect to the interpretation and enforcement of the provisions of the A&R LPA, including Section 8.04 and the fiduciary duties of the General Partner, will apply the substantive law of the State of Delaware. Nothing in this Section 7 is intended to alter the governing law of the A&R LPA or any other agreement to which the Clients are a party.

**[8. Conflicts of Interest]{.underline}**

C&H has conducted a conflicts check in accordance with the Firm\'s standard procedures and the applicable rules of professional conduct. Based on the results of that check, C&H confirms that it is not aware of any current conflict of interest that would preclude the Firm from undertaking this engagement on behalf of the Clients.

C&H confirms that it does not currently represent any limited partner of the Fund, any member of the Investor Advisory Committee, or the IAC\'s counsel, Wexford Crane & Albright LLP, in any matter related to the Fund, DCM, or the Key Person Event. C&H may represent other clients in matters unrelated to this engagement, and the Clients acknowledge that such representations do not constitute a conflict of interest for purposes of this engagement.

In the event that a conflict of interest arises during the course of this engagement, C&H will promptly notify the Clients and take appropriate steps in accordance with the applicable rules of professional conduct governing attorneys admitted to practice in the State of New York, including, where appropriate, seeking a waiver of the conflict or, if necessary, withdrawing from the engagement.

**[9. Confidentiality]{.underline}**

C&H will maintain the confidentiality of all information received from or on behalf of the Clients in connection with this engagement, consistent with the Firm\'s professional responsibility obligations under the applicable rules of professional conduct and the protections afforded by the attorney-client privilege and the work product doctrine. C&H will implement reasonable safeguards to protect the confidentiality of such information within the Firm.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, C&H may disclose confidential information: (a) as required by applicable law, regulation, or court order; (b) as authorized or directed by the Clients; or (c) to the extent reasonably necessary in connection with the performance of the services described in this engagement letter, including, without limitation, in communications with the Administrator, counsel to the IAC, or other third parties as directed by the Clients.

**[10. Document Retention]{.underline}**

Upon completion of the engagement, C&H will retain client files (including electronic files) in accordance with the Firm\'s document retention policy, which currently provides for retention of engagement files for a period of ten (10) years from the date of engagement closure. Following the expiration of such retention period, C&H may destroy or dispose of the engagement files without further notice to or consent from the Clients, unless the Clients have previously requested the return of such files.

Original documents provided by the Clients to C&H during the course of this engagement will be returned to the Clients upon written request. C&H may retain copies of such original documents in accordance with the retention policy described above.

**[11. Termination]{.underline}**

Either party may terminate this engagement at any time upon thirty (30) days\' prior written notice to the other party. In the event of termination by either party, the Clients will remain responsible for payment of all fees and disbursements incurred by C&H through the effective date of termination, subject to the Fee Cap set forth in Section 6.2.

Upon termination, C&H will cooperate in the orderly transition of the matter to successor counsel designated by the Clients, including the prompt delivery of all work product, client files, and other materials in C&H\'s possession that are necessary for successor counsel to continue the representation. C&H\'s obligation to assist in the orderly transition of the matter shall survive the termination of this engagement.

**[12. Acceptance]{.underline}**

We would appreciate it if you would confirm the Clients\' acceptance of the terms set forth in this engagement letter by signing and returning a copy of this letter to the undersigned at your earliest convenience. This engagement shall be deemed to have commenced as of June 11, 2024, upon your execution of this letter. If you have any questions regarding the terms of this engagement, please do not hesitate to contact either of the undersigned.

We look forward to working with you and the Driftwood team on this important matter.

Very truly yours,

**CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP**

Fundraise Timeline. The GP targets a First Close on or about January 15, 2026, with a Final Close deadline of July 15, 2026. Pursuant to the Fund's limited partnership agreement (the "LPA"), the GP is required to deliver a redacted compilation of all side letter terms (the "MFN Side Letter Compilation") to eligible limited partners within fifteen (15) business days following the Final Close. A thirty (30) calendar day MFN election period commences upon delivery of the Compilation, during which eligible subsequent limited partners may elect to adopt any MFN-eligible provision granted to any other limited partner.

Each anchor LP's commitment and fee terms were negotiated in connection with the Fund's first closing process and are set forth in individual side letters executed concurrently with such LP's subscription agreement and joinder to the LPA. CPERS is represented by Whitfield & Gage LLP in connection with its commitment. NEP is represented by Hollander McKee & Stone LLP. Brindoval is represented by Prescott & Langley LLP. Each of these firms has extensive experience in fund formation and side letter negotiations, and each has demonstrated familiarity with MFN election mechanics and the scope of MFN-eligible provisions in prior fund transactions.

It should be noted that the MFN Threshold applies to the aggregate commitment of a limited partner, not to the commitment of affiliated vehicles. The LPA does not currently aggregate commitments of affiliated investors for purposes of the MFN Threshold. Owen and Nicholas may wish to consider whether the LPA should be amended prior to First Close to include an aggregation provision, which could either expand or restrict the MFN-eligible pool depending on the composition of the subsequent LP base.
•  Final Close: July 15, 2026 (the deadline for the admission of additional limited partners to the Fund).

•  MFN Side Letter Compilation: The GP is required to prepare and deliver to each MFN-eligible limited partner a redacted compilation of all side letter provisions granted to any limited partner, excluding (a) the identity of the limited partner to which each provision was originally granted and (b) Excluded Provisions. The Compilation must be delivered within fifteen (15) business days after the Final Close.

The practical implication of this timeline is significant for budget planning purposes. Assuming the Final Close occurs on July 15, 2026, the Compilation would be delivered on or about August 5, 2026 (fifteen business days later), and the MFN election period would close on or about September 4, 2026. The GP will therefore not have full visibility into the extent of MFN fee elections — and thus the Fund's actual management fee revenue for the first year of the investment period — until nearly eight months after the targeted First Close and approximately two months after the Final Close. During this period, the GP should budget conservatively, assuming a worst-case fee scenario consistent with Scenario 1 in Section IV.B below.

Limitations. The LPA's fee structure would need to be finalized before or at the First Close on January 15, 2026. This requires coordination with Rajesh Mehta and Claire Dubois to determine whether commitment-based fee tiers are commercially acceptable and whether the proposed tier breakpoints and rates are consistent with the GP's fundraising strategy. Additionally, the tier structure would need to be disclosed to all prospective limited partners during the fundraise, which could affect commitment dynamics — some LPs might increase their commitments to reach a lower fee tier, while others might view the tiered structure as evidence that fee negotiation is possible and seek additional concessions.
We recommend discussing this option with Rajesh Mehta and Claire Dubois at the earliest opportunity, given the First Close timeline.

The MFN election process occurs after the Final Close, providing the GP with visibility into the full LP base before the MFN Side Letter Compilation is prepared and delivered. We recommend the following timing-related measures:

2.  Commitment-Based Fee Tiers. Evaluate the feasibility of converting fee concessions from ad hoc side letter provisions to LPA-level commitment-based tiers before the First Close on January 15, 2026. This approach requires amendment of the LPA's fee provisions and must be coordinated with Rajesh Mehta and Claire Dubois, as it affects the Fund's marketing and fundraising strategy. If the tier approach is adopted, the CPERS and NEP side letters will need to be revised to remove the fee concession provisions and instead reference the LPA fee schedule.
### documents/matters/1002-00003/Memos & Analyses/side-letter-strategy-and-mfn-framework-memo.docx

Each of these anchor investors will execute a separate side letter agreement that supplements the Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement of Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP (the "LPA"), which is expected to be dated as of the First Close on January 15, 2026. The side letters will grant various economic, governance, informational, and operational accommodations tailored to the legal status, investment policy requirements, and negotiating priorities of each anchor LP.

The key timeline milestones are as follows: initial drafts of the three anchor side letters are targeted for distribution to counterparty counsel by October 20, 2025; the negotiation period is expected to extend through December 20, 2025 (with two to three rounds of mark-ups anticipated per side letter); the First Close is targeted for January 15, 2026; and the Final Close deadline is July 15, 2026. The MFN Side Letter Compilation will be delivered to all MFN-eligible limited partners within fifteen (15) business days following the Final Close.

The Fund will rely on the exemption from registration under the Investment Company Act of 1940, as amended, pursuant to either Section 3(c)(1) (limiting the Fund to no more than 100 beneficial owners) or Section 3(c)(7) (limiting the Fund to "qualified purchasers" as defined in Section 2(a)(51) of the Investment Company Act). The determination of which exemption will be relied upon will depend on the composition and number of investors admitted through the Final Close. Given the target fund size and the anticipated investor base, we expect the Fund to rely primarily on Section 3(c)(7).

Target Fund Size and Hard Cap. The Fund's target aggregate capital commitments are $600,000,000. The LPA provides for a hard cap of $750,000,000, above which no additional commitments may be accepted without the consent of a majority-in-interest of the existing limited partners. The $150,000,000 buffer between the target and the hard cap provides meaningful flexibility for the GP to accommodate additional investor interest, particularly from institutional investors who may increase their commitments following the First Close.

Carried Interest. The GP is entitled to a carried interest of 20% of net profits over an 8% preferred return (compounded annually). The LPA provides for a 100% GP catch-up to a 20/80 split once the preferred return has been fully distributed. Thereafter, all distributions are split 80% to the limited partners and 20% to the GP. The carried interest structure is standard for venture capital funds and is not a point of significant negotiation with the anchor LPs.

Fund Term. The Fund has a term of ten (10) years from the First Close, with a scheduled termination date of January 15, 2036. The LPA provides the GP with discretion to extend the term for up to two (2) additional one-year periods (i.e., through January 15, 2037, and if further extended, through January 15, 2038), subject to the GP's good faith determination that such extensions are necessary or desirable to facilitate the orderly liquidation of remaining portfolio investments.

The remaining commitments needed to reach the target fund size of $600,000,000 total $435,000,000. Based on the GP's current pipeline and Greystone's placement efforts, the GP expects to secure an additional $250,000,000 to $350,000,000 in commitments from institutional investors (pension funds, endowments, foundations, fund-of-funds, and insurance company general accounts) and $85,000,000 to $185,000,000 from family offices and high-net-worth investors, with a Final Close target of July 15, 2026.

The MFN framework will be implemented as follows: each anchor side letter will include an MFN election right provision, and the same provision (or a substantively identical provision) will be included in the side letters of all subsequent LPs whose commitments meet or exceed the MFN eligibility threshold. Separately, the GP will prepare a template MFN Election Procedures Letter and MFN Election Form, which will be distributed as part of the side letter package following the Final Close. All side letters, the LPA, and the MFN framework documents will be governed by the laws of the State of Delaware.

Following the Final Close of the Fund (targeted for July 15, 2026), the GP will prepare a redacted compilation of all side letter terms granted to any limited partner of the Fund (the "MFN Side Letter Compilation"). The compilation will be structured as a single reference document organized by provision category, and will be subject to the following parameters:

•  Delivery deadline. The GP will deliver the MFN Side Letter Compilation to all MFN-eligible limited partners within fifteen (15) business days following the Final Close. Assuming a Final Close date of July 15, 2026, and accounting for weekends and typical summer holidays, the practical deadline for delivery of the compilation is approximately August 5, 2026.

3.  Sunset provision. Consider including a "sunset" mechanism providing that MFN elections apply only to side letter terms granted before the Final Close, and do not extend to amendments, supplements, or side letters entered into after the MFN Election Period. This prevents the GP from being locked into an MFN framework indefinitely and preserves flexibility for post-closing accommodations.

•  Uniform LPA cross-references. All side letters should contain a uniform cross-reference to the governing agreement: "This Side Letter supplements the Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement of Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP, dated as of January 15, 2026 (as may be further amended, restated, supplemented, or otherwise modified from time to time, the 'LPA')." Any amendments to the LPA after the First Close should be reflected in a corresponding update to the side letter cross-reference.

•  Key-person provisions. The LPA designates Rajesh Mehta and Claire Dubois as "Key Persons" and addresses the consequences of a key-person event, including a potential suspension of the investment period. The side letter provision (granting enhanced notification rights) should be drafted to supplement the LPA's key-person provisions without creating inconsistent obligations. For example, the LPA may require notice to all limited partners within ten (10) business days of a key-person event, while the side letter may require notice to NEP within five (5) business days. The side letter should be drafted to acknowledge the LPA's baseline notice requirement and to impose an accelerated timeline for the side letter LP only.

Re: Legal Opinion — Securities Act and Investment Company Act Compliance Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP — First Close

We have acted as fund formation counsel to Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (the "Sponsor"), Harrowgate Fund V GP LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (the "General Partner"), and Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP, a Delaware limited partnership (the "Fund" or "HPE Fund V"), in connection with the formation of the Fund and the offering and sale of limited partnership interests in the Fund (the "Interests") to certain investors (each, a "Limited Partner" or "Investor" and, collectively, the "Limited Partners" or "Investors"). This opinion letter (this "Opinion") is delivered at, and as of the date of, the initial closing of the Fund (the "First Close"), which is occurring on the date hereof. This Opinion is being delivered to you in connection with, and at your request in anticipation of, the First Close.

1.1 The Agreement of Limited Partnership of Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP (the "LPA"), dated as of the date hereof, by and among the General Partner and each of the Limited Partners admitted to the Fund as of the First Close;

1.6 The form of Subscription Agreement executed by each Limited Partner admitted at the First Close (each, a "Subscription Agreement"), including the Investor Questionnaire attached thereto as Exhibit A (the "Investor Questionnaire"), together with all schedules, annexes, and supplements thereto;

1.7 Each executed side letter agreement between the General Partner (or, as applicable, the Fund) and individual Limited Partners admitted at the First Close (collectively, the "Side Letters"), setting forth certain modifications, waivers, or supplemental terms applicable to such Limited Partners;
1.8 The executed Subscription Agreements and related documentation for each of the following Limited Partners admitted at the First Close, which we have individually reviewed:

1.9 The Form D (Notice of Exempt Offering of Securities) prepared for filing with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (the "SEC") within fifteen (15) days of the First Close pursuant to Rule 503 of Regulation D under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the "Securities Act");
With respect to each Investor admitted as a Limited Partner at the First Close, we have assumed the following:

(d) That the offering and sale of the Interests has been conducted solely in compliance with the requirements of Regulation D, Rule 506(b), promulgated under the Securities Act, and that no more than thirty-five (35) non-accredited investors (within the meaning of Rule 501(a) of Regulation D) have purchased Interests in the offering. We understand, based on our review of the executed Subscription Agreements and Investor Questionnaires, and based on representations of the General Partner, that all Investors admitted at the First Close are accredited investors within the meaning of Rule 501(a) and qualified purchasers within the meaning of Section 2(a)(51) of the 1940 Act.

(a) That the Fund will timely file a Form D (Notice of Exempt Offering of Securities) with the SEC within fifteen (15) calendar days following the First Close, in accordance with the requirements of Rule 503 of Regulation D, and will file any required amendments to such Form D in a timely manner thereafter, including amendments to reflect any subsequent closings and any material changes in the information reported therein.

(b) That the Fund will make all required notice filings (commonly referred to as "blue sky" filings) under the securities laws of each state and territory of the United States in which any Investor admitted at the First Close is domiciled or maintains its principal place of business, to the extent required by the applicable state securities laws and regulations. We understand that many states have adopted Regulation D coordination or notification exemptions (including, without limitation, exemptions under uniform limited offering exemptions modeled on or substantially similar to the National Securities Markets Improvement Act of 1996 ("NSMIA") preemption provisions applicable to "covered securities" under Section 18 of the Securities Act), and that the Fund intends to rely on such exemptions and make all required notice filings in connection therewith.

(c) That the Fund will not, following the First Close, take any action, or permit any condition to exist, that would cause the offering and sale of the Interests to fail to satisfy the conditions and requirements of Rule 506(b) of Regulation D or Section 4(a)(2) of the Securities Act, including without limitation (i) engaging in any form of general solicitation or general advertising in connection with the offering, (ii) admitting any Investor who is not an accredited investor and a qualified purchaser, (iii) failing to provide adequate information to any Investor as required by Regulation D, or (iv) permitting any covered person to become subject to a disqualifying event under Rule 506(d).

(d) That the aggregate capital commitments to the Fund at the First Close are Seven Hundred Fifty Million Dollars ($750,000,000), and that the Fund's target fundraise is One Billion Five Hundred Million Dollars ($1,500,000,000), with a hard cap of One Billion Seven Hundred Fifty Million Dollars ($1,750,000,000) (inclusive of the General Partner commitment), and that subsequent closings may be held on a rolling basis until the Final Close Deadline of February 15, 2027 (eighteen months following the First Close).

Based on the foregoing review of the Reviewed Documents and subject to the Assumptions, qualifications, and limitations set forth herein, it is our opinion that the offering and sale of the Interests in the Fund, as described in the PPM, the LPA, and the Subscription Agreements, and as conducted through the First Close, are exempt from the registration requirements of Section 5 of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the "Securities Act"), pursuant to Section 4(a)(2) of the Securities Act and Rule 506(b) of Regulation D promulgated thereunder (17 C.F.R. §§ 230.501–230.508).

(b) Accredited Investor Status. The Interests have been offered and sold only to persons who are "accredited investors" as defined in Rule 501(a) of Regulation D. Each Investor admitted at the First Close has represented and warranted in its Subscription Agreement and Investor Questionnaire that it meets the requirements of one or more of the categories of accredited investors enumerated in Rule 501(a), and the General Partner has verified such status through its review of the Investor Questionnaires and related documentation. No non-accredited investors have been admitted to the Fund at the First Close.

(c) Investment Intent. Each Investor admitted at the First Close has represented and warranted in its Subscription Agreement that it is acquiring the Interests for its own account for investment purposes only and not with a view to distribution within the meaning of the Securities Act. Each Investor has further acknowledged the restrictions on transferability of the Interests and the absence of any public market for the Interests.

(d) Access to Information. Each Investor admitted at the First Close has been provided with, or has had access to, all material information concerning the Fund, the General Partner, and the Sponsor, including the PPM, the LPA, and the opportunity to ask questions of, and receive answers from, representatives of the General Partner and the Sponsor. The PPM contains detailed information regarding the Fund's investment strategy, the terms and conditions of the Interests, the risks associated with an investment in the Fund, the management and advisory fees payable by the Fund, and other material information.

(e) Number of Purchasers. The number of purchasers of the Interests at the First Close (six Investors, as identified in Section 1.8 above) does not exceed the maximum number of purchasers permitted under Rule 506(b) of Regulation D, which limits non-accredited investors to thirty-five (35) but imposes no limit on the number of accredited investors.

Based on the foregoing review of the Reviewed Documents and subject to the Assumptions, qualifications, and limitations set forth herein, it is our opinion that the Fund is not, and upon the consummation of the First Close and the admission of the Limited Partners will not be, required to register as an "investment company" under the Investment Company Act of 1940, as amended (the "1940 Act"), by reason of the exclusion from the definition of "investment company" provided by Section 3(c)(7) of the 1940 Act.

(a) Qualified Purchaser Requirement. The outstanding securities of the Fund (i.e., the Interests) are, and upon consummation of the First Close will be, owned exclusively by persons who, at the time of acquisition of such securities, are "qualified purchasers" within the meaning of Section 2(a)(51) of the 1940 Act and Rule 2a51-1 promulgated thereunder. Each Investor admitted at the First Close has represented and warranted in its Subscription Agreement and Investor Questionnaire that it is a "qualified purchaser" within the meaning of Section 2(a)(51) of the 1940 Act, and the General Partner has verified such status through its review of the Investor Questionnaires and related documentation.

(d) Minimum Commitment. The minimum capital commitment for each Limited Partner admitted to the Fund is Ten Million Dollars ($10,000,000), subject to waiver by the General Partner in its sole discretion. Impact on Tidewater Sovereign Investment Authority. Tidewater's $175,000,000 commitment will be made through the Offshore Feeder (the Cayman-domiciled vehicle), as Tidewater has indicated a preference for investing through a non-U.S. structure for tax and regulatory reasons. If the Offshore Feeder is not a party to the Facility — either as a co-borrower or as a pledgor/guarantor — Tidewater's $175,000,000 commitment will not be included in the Main Fund's borrowing base. This would reduce the estimated borrowing base at First Close by approximately $157,500,000 (90% of $175,000,000), a material reduction that would meaningfully limit the Fund's borrowing capacity during the early stages of the investment period when Facility availability is most critical.

At the First Close minimum of $750,000,000 in aggregate commitments, 25% of uncalled commitments equals $187,500,000. At First Close, the Facility availability will be constrained by both the LPA leverage limit and the borrowing base calculation, with the more restrictive of the two constraints governing. If the estimated borrowing base at First Close is approximately $472,500,000 (as calculated in Section II.E above, assuming Tidewater is included), the binding constraint at First Close will be the LPA leverage limit of $187,500,000, not the borrowing base. This means that the Fund will have access to significantly less than the full $500,000,000 Facility commitment during the early stages of the investment period, with availability increasing as additional LPs are admitted in subsequent closings.

We have not identified any inconsistency between the LPA leverage limit and the Facility terms. However, we recommend confirming that the LPA leverage limit is measured against "aggregate uncalled commitments" across all Fund vehicles — including the Main Fund, the Parallel Fund, and the Offshore Feeder — rather than Main Fund commitments only. If the leverage limit is measured on a Main Fund-only basis, the available leverage headroom will be significantly lower than if it is measured on an aggregate cross-vehicle basis. The LPA drafting should clarify this point.

We note that the LPA's waterfall provisions — governing the distribution of investment proceeds among return of capital, preferred return, and carried interest — are not directly affected by the use of the Facility. The waterfall calculations are based on aggregate capital contributed and distributed, regardless of the timing of capital calls. However, the timing of capital calls does affect performance metric calculations, particularly internal rate of return ("IRR"). By using the Facility to bridge investments and delaying the corresponding capital calls, the Fund effectively reduces the period during which LP capital is outstanding, which mechanically increases the reported IRR. This IRR enhancement effect is well recognized in the private equity industry and has been the subject of significant commentary from institutional LP groups, including the Institutional Limited Partners Association ("ILPA").

3.2 LPAC Composition. The LPAC shall consist of five (5) members, each of whom shall be a designee of a limited partner of the Fund selected by the General Partner in consultation with the limited partners. Three (3) LPAC members, including the Limited Partner's designated representative, shall be designated at or prior to the First Close. The remaining two (2) LPAC members shall be designated on or before the Final Close. The Limited Partner's designated representative shall serve from the First Close for the duration of the Fund Term, subject to the Limited Partner's right to replace its designated representative at any time by delivering written notice to the General Partner identifying the replacement representative. Such replacement shall be effective upon the General Partner's receipt of such notice (or such later date as may be specified therein).

3.3 Alternate Representative. The Limited Partner may designate an alternate representative to attend any LPAC meeting in the event that the primary representative designated pursuant to Section 3.1 is unavailable due to scheduling conflicts, illness, or other circumstances. The Limited Partner shall provide prior written notice to the General Partner (including via electronic mail) of the identity of the alternate representative reasonably in advance of the applicable LPAC meeting. Such alternate representative shall have the same rights and authority as the primary representative with respect to the applicable meeting, including the right to vote on matters presented to the LPAC.

3.4 Scope and Governance. The LPAC shall operate in accordance with the LPAC Charter and Terms of Reference (the "LPAC Charter") adopted by the Fund, a copy of which has been provided to the Limited Partner. Recommendation: We recommend that the Fund structure its subscription facility drawdowns as short-term bridge financing, with a target repayment period of fewer than sixty (60) days. This approach is designed to minimize the duration of any indebtedness that could be characterized as acquisition indebtedness and to limit the ratio of debt-financed basis to total basis for purposes of the IRC §514 calculation. The LPA should include provisions that align the subscription facility terms with this approach and that empower the General Partner to manage drawdowns in a manner that minimizes UBTI exposure for tax-exempt investors. If the Fund requires longer-term borrowing to complete an acquisition or bridge a capital call during a period of market disruption, the General Partner should consult with tax counsel before drawing down the facility for a period exceeding sixty (60) days.

Recommendation: We recommend that the Fund maintain separate tracking of all UBTI-generating activities at the Fund level for reporting purposes. The LPA should include appropriate language requiring the General Partner to provide UBTI-related information in the annual tax packages delivered to investors. The K-1 reporting system implemented by Halcyon Fund Services should be designed to identify and separately report each UBTI component, including the source activity, to enable tax-exempt investors to comply with the silo rule. We also recommend including a provision in the LPA's tax reporting section that obligates the Fund to provide UBTI information in a format consistent with the silo rule requirements.

The distinction between organizational and syndication costs is a factual determination that must be made based on the nature of each expense. Many expenses incurred in connection with a fund formation have elements of both categories (e.g., legal fees may relate to both the drafting of the LPA (organizational) and the preparation of the PPM (syndication)). Proper classification is important because the tax treatment differs significantly.

Each of the representations and warranties set forth in this Article 2 shall be deemed to be continuing representations and warranties made by the Subscriber for the benefit of the Partnership and the General Partner and shall be deemed to be repeated by the Subscriber (a) at the time of each Capital Call, (b) at each closing (including the First Close and any Subsequent Close) at which the Subscriber is admitted as a limited partner or at which the Subscriber's Capital Commitment is increased, and (c) at such other times as the General Partner may reasonably request. The Subscriber agrees to promptly notify the General Partner in writing if any representation or warranty made herein becomes inaccurate or misleading in any material respect.
"Closing" means the First Close, any Subsequent Close, or the Final Close, as applicable.
"Final Close" means the final closing of the Fund, anticipated to occur on or about May 15, 2027, or such later date as the General Partner may determine in its sole discretion.
"First Close" means the initial closing of the Fund, anticipated to occur on or about November 15, 2026, subject to receipt of aggregate Capital Commitments of not less than $250,000,000.

"Investment Period" means the period commencing on the date of the First Close and ending on the earlier of (i) the fifth anniversary of the First Close, (ii) the date on which the General Partner determines that the Fund's uninvested Capital Commitments have been fully invested or reserved, or (iii) such earlier date as may be specified in the Partnership Agreement.
"Subsequent Close" means any closing of the Fund occurring after the First Close and prior to the Final Close.

WHEREAS, on or about October 28, 2022, the Portland Metropolitan Water District (the "Water District") notified the Company of its intent to renegotiate the forty (40)-year water-treatment concession for the Bull Run Filtration Project (originally executed in approximately 2018) (the "Concession"), citing changed regulatory requirements under Oregon Senate Bill 1567 (2022), and the renegotiation of the Concession (the "Concession Renegotiation") contributed to the suspension of the Transaction and the declaration of a Material Impediment Event under Section 7.04 of the Limited Partnership Agreement of ICM Cascadia Co-Invest, LP, dated July 29, 2022 (the "Co-Invest LP Agreement"), on January 9, 2023, and the Concession Renegotiation remains pending as of the date hereof;

January 9, 2023. After receiving additional information regarding the scope of PMWD's renegotiation demands — which indicated that PMWD was seeking substantial rate reductions, enhanced performance guarantees, and significant capital-upgrade obligations to be borne by Cascadia — the GP determined that the concession renegotiation constituted a Material Impediment Event under Section 7.04 of the Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement of ICM Cascadia Co-Invest, LP (the "LP Agreement"). The GP issued a formal declaration of a Material Impediment Event and simultaneously issued a capital-call suspension notice, effectively placing the Vehicle into dormancy. •  Limited Partnership Agreement of ICM Cascadia Co-Invest, LP (the "LP Agreement"), dated as of July 29, 2022, by and between Meridian Infrastructure GP IV LLC, as general partner, and Ironside Capital Management LP, as limited partner, governed by the laws of the State of Delaware.
Wind-Down Election Right of Ironside Capital Management LP Under §7.04(c) of the Limited Partnership Agreement of ICM Cascadia Co-Invest, LP — Analysis of the 18-Month Dormancy Trigger

This memorandum analyzes the contractual right of Ironside Capital Management LP ("Ironside" or the "LP") under Section 7.04(c) of the Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement, dated July 29, 2022 (the "LP Agreement"), of ICM Cascadia Co-Invest, LP (the "Vehicle"), to elect a wind-down of the Vehicle following eighteen (18) continuous months of dormancy. The LP Agreement governs the rights and obligations of the Vehicle's two partners: Meridian Infrastructure GP IV LLC (the "GP"), serving as general partner, and Ironside, serving as the sole limited partner.

The Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement was executed on July 29, 2022 and is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to conflicts-of-law principles that would require the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction.

Nature of the Right. The wind-down election right is a unilateral right of the LP. Exercise does not require the consent, approval, or concurrence of the GP. The GP has no veto or blocking right with respect to the LP's election. Nor is the exercise of the right subject to the approval of any advisory committee, investor committee, or other governance body of the Vehicle or of Fund IV. The right is, in plain terms, a "put" option held by the LP that, upon exercise, obligates the GP to commence an orderly wind-down of the Vehicle in accordance with §7.05.

This memorandum has been prepared by Calderwood & Harkness LLP, in its capacity as fund counsel to Driftwood Capital Management LLC ("DCM" or the "General Partner") and Driftwood Absolute Return Fund Ltd. ("DARF" or the "Fund"), at the request of DCM, to brief the Investor Advisory Committee (the "IAC") in advance of its meeting scheduled for July 29, 2024.

(iv) the IAC's specific role in the proposed successor governance framework, including the designation of an independent member to the newly created three-member Investment Committee, and the significance of the IAC members' collective voting weight in the LP consent solicitation.

We note that IAC counsel, Wexford Crane & Albright LLP ("WCA"), specifically Helen M. Calloway, Partner, and David Pineda, Senior Associate, has been provided with copies of all materials referenced herein, including the draft First Amendment, the Successor Key Person Proposal, and all supporting documentation. WCA is independently reviewing the proposed amendment on behalf of the IAC and is expected to provide its comments and recommendations to the IAC members separately. This memorandum is prepared by Calderwood & Harkness LLP in its capacity as fund counsel and does not purport to serve as independent legal advice to the IAC or any individual IAC member. Each IAC member should consult with its own legal counsel and with WCA as appropriate.

Key Person Event. Marcus J. Whitmore, Founder, Chief Investment Officer, and sole designated "Key Person" under Section 8.04(a) of the A&R LPA, suffered a severe hemorrhagic stroke on June 3, 2024. Mr. Whitmore has been unable to perform any professional duties since that date, and his physicians have projected a minimum twelve- to eighteen-month recovery period with an uncertain return-to-work prognosis. Pursuant to Section 8.04(b) of the A&R LPA, a Key Person Event was deemed triggered on June 10, 2024, upon the expiration of seven consecutive calendar days during which Mr. Whitmore was unable to devote substantially all of his professional time to the affairs of the Fund.

Consequences Triggered. Immediately upon the occurrence of the Key Person Event, the consequences prescribed by Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA took effect, including: (a) an immediate suspension of the Investment Period, pursuant to which no new investments may be made by the Fund; (b) a cap on follow-on investments of $28.7 million, representing 1.0% of the Fund's assets under management as of the trigger date; and (c) the commencement of a ninety-calendar-day Cure Period, which began on June 10, 2024 and is scheduled to expire on September 8, 2024.

LP Notification. The General Partner sent written notification of the Key Person Event to all limited partners on June 14, 2024, which was within the contractual five-business-day deadline prescribed by Section 8.04(c)(iii) of the A&R LPA. The required deadline for such notification was June 17, 2024, and the General Partner's notice was therefore timely delivered.

Successor Key Person Proposal. On July 15, 2024, the General Partner circulated to all forty-seven limited partners of the Fund the Successor Key Person Proposal (the "Proposal"), together with a draft First Amendment to the A&R LPA. The Proposal designates Elaine R. Sato, Deputy Chief Investment Officer and Managing Member (10%) of DCM, and Jonathan K. Huang, Head of Credit Strategies at DCM, as joint Successor Key Persons. The Proposal further introduces a series of governance enhancements, including the creation of a three-member Investment Committee.

IAC Role. The proposed amendment would empower the IAC to designate one independent member to the newly created three-member Investment Committee, representing a material governance enhancement and a new fiduciary check on the General Partner's investment discretion. The five IAC members collectively hold $1,140 million in voting LP capital commitments, representing approximately 40.7% of total voting LP commitments, and their collective support is therefore a critical — though not independently sufficient — factor in achieving the required 66⅔% consent threshold.

Mr. Whitmore has served as the sole designated Key Person under the A&R LPA since the inception of the Fund. Ms. Sato has served as Deputy CIO and has been a managing member of DCM since the Fund's formation. The governance structure of DCM and the allocation of authority between the managing members are governed by the Operating Agreement of Driftwood Capital Management LLC, which is not directly at issue in this memorandum but is relevant to the proposed carried interest reallocation discussed in Section VII.F below.

The investment team, led by Ms. Sato and Mr. Huang in the absence of Mr. Whitmore, has maintained strong positioning across all three strategy verticals notwithstanding the occurrence of the Key Person Event. The Fund's year-to-date net return of +5.4% compares favorably to its peer group, and the current NAV per unit of $150.53 exceeds the high-water mark of $142.67 by approximately 5.5%, indicating that the incentive allocation mechanism remains "in the money" for the General Partner. The Fund's gross leverage of 1.85× and net exposure of 0.60× are within the Fund's stated risk parameters as set forth in the A&R LPA and the Fund's offering memorandum.

Mr. Whitmore is the sole designated "Key Person" under Section 8.04(a) of the A&R LPA, dated March 15, 2017. The designation of Mr. Whitmore as the sole Key Person reflected his foundational role in the Fund's investment strategy, his personal relationships with the Fund's institutional investor base, and his singular authority over all material investment decisions during the Fund's operating history.

Based on information provided by Mr. Whitmore's medical team to the General Partner, Mr. Whitmore's physicians project a minimum twelve- to eighteen-month recovery period. The return-to-work prognosis remains uncertain, and Mr. Whitmore's physicians have indicated that even upon completion of rehabilitation, Mr. Whitmore's ability to resume the full scope of his prior professional responsibilities cannot be assured at this time. The General Partner has engaged an independent medical consultant to provide periodic updates to the Fund's limited partners regarding Mr. Whitmore's recovery status, consistent with the General Partner's obligations of good faith and fair dealing under the A&R LPA.

Section 8.04(b) of the A&R LPA provides that a Key Person Event is deemed to have occurred if the Key Person is "unable to devote substantially all of his professional time to the affairs of the Partnership for a period of seven (7) consecutive calendar days," absent prior written notice to the limited partners that the Key Person anticipates such an absence. The provision is self-executing: no action by the General Partner, the limited partners, or the IAC is required to trigger the Key Person Event; rather, the event is deemed to have occurred automatically upon the satisfaction of the seven-consecutive-calendar-day condition.

A Key Person Event was therefore deemed triggered on June 10, 2024, pursuant to Section 8.04(b) of the A&R LPA. This determination has been confirmed by Calderwood & Harkness LLP, as fund counsel, and has not been disputed by any party.

Investment Period Suspension. The Investment Period, as defined in Section 1.01 of the A&R LPA, was immediately suspended as of June 10, 2024. During the suspension, no new investments may be made by the Fund. This suspension remains in effect as of the date of this memorandum and will continue until the Key Person Event is cured in accordance with the A&R LPA or, if not cured, until the Fund is wound down.

LP Notification. Section 8.04(c)(iii) of the A&R LPA requires the General Partner to notify all limited partners in writing within five (5) business days of the occurrence of a Key Person Event. A copy of the LP Notification Letter is included as Attachment E to this memorandum.

The General Partner has proposed the designation of two individuals as joint Successor Key Persons under the A&R LPA, as amended by the proposed First Amendment. The following is a summary of the key terms and provisions of the proposed First Amendment to the A&R LPA, as set forth in the draft circulated to all limited partners on July 15, 2024. A complete copy of the draft First Amendment is included as Attachment B to this memorandum. This summary is qualified in its entirety by reference to the full text of the draft First Amendment.

IX. Role of the IAC in the Proposed Governance Framework

As described in Section VII.C above, the proposed First Amendment would empower the IAC to designate one independent member to the three-member Investment Committee. This independent member would serve alongside Ms. Sato (as Chair) and Mr. Huang, and the Investment Committee would exercise oversight authority over all new investments exceeding the threshold specified in the First Amendment. Wexford Crane & Albright LLP, specifically Helen M. Calloway, Partner, and David Pineda, Senior Associate, has been retained by the IAC to independently review the proposed First Amendment and to advise the IAC on the legal, governance, and economic implications of the Proposal. WCA has been provided with complete copies of all materials distributed to the limited partners, including the draft First Amendment, the Successor Key Person Proposal letter, the LP Notification letter, and all supporting documentation.

The A&R LPA is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, as specified in Section 15.08 thereof. The following is a summary of certain Delaware law considerations relevant to the proposed First Amendment and the LP consent solicitation. This summary is not exhaustive and is provided for informational purposes only.

Fiduciary Duties. Under the Delaware Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act (6 Del. C. §§ 17-101 et seq.) (the "DRULPA"), the general partner of a Delaware limited partnership owes fiduciary duties to the limited partners, including the duty of loyalty and the duty of care, unless such duties are modified or eliminated by the partnership agreement. (b) Establishment of a Three-Member Investment Committee. C&H recommended the creation of a formal Investment Committee under a new Section 8.05 of the A&R LPA. The Investment Committee was to be composed of three members: Sato (as Chair), Huang, and one independent member to be designated by the Investor Advisory Committee. The inclusion of an IAC-designated independent member was intended to enhance governance credibility and LP confidence, and to provide an institutional check on investment decision-making in the absence of Whitmore.

(e) Marcus J. Whitmore — Senior Advisor Designation. C&H recommended that Whitmore be transitioned to a "Senior Advisor" role with no governance authority under the A&R LPA as amended. Whitmore would retain no voting rights, no investment approval authority, and no management decision-making power with respect to the Fund. This designation was intended to preserve Whitmore's association with the Fund in a manner appropriate to his medical circumstances while making clear to the LP base that active governance authority had been fully transferred to the Successor Key Persons and the Investment Committee.

Drafting of the First Amendment. Based on the approved governance framework, C&H drafted the First Amendment to the A&R LPA, incorporating all of the recommended structural changes. C&H also prepared the Successor Key Person Proposal and Consent Solicitation Letter to the limited partners (the "Successor Proposal Letter"), which set forth the rationale for the proposed successor governance framework, summarized the key terms of the First Amendment, and enclosed the Form of LP Written Consent.

The memorandum was distributed to the five members of the Investor Advisory Committee, who collectively represented $1,140 million in capital commitments to the Fund. The IAC members, their affiliations, and their respective capital commitments were as follows:

The IAC Briefing Memorandum described the circumstances of the Key Person Event, the contractual consequences, the successor governance framework recommended by C&H and adopted by DCM, the key terms of the proposed First Amendment, and the consent solicitation process and timeline. The memorandum also included background information on the proposed Successor Key Persons, including their professional experience, roles at DCM, capital commitments to the Fund, and proposed carried interest allocations.

July 29, 2024 — IAC Meeting. A formal meeting of the Investor Advisory Committee was held on July 29, 2024 by videoconference. The meeting was attended by all five IAC members and their respective representatives, as well as Graham Sutherland and Stephen Adler of C&H (on behalf of DCM) and Helen M. Calloway and David Pineda of Wexford Crane & Albright LLP (as counsel to the IAC). Elaine R. Sato and Jonathan K. Huang of DCM also participated in portions of the meeting to present their respective backgrounds, investment philosophies, and plans for the ongoing management of the Fund. The IAC meeting lasted approximately two and one-half hours and included a detailed discussion of the proposed governance framework, the qualifications of the Successor Key Persons, the scope of the independent Investment Committee member's authority, and the LP consent solicitation process.

WCA Comments and Negotiation. Following the IAC meeting, Wexford Crane & Albright LLP, acting on behalf of the IAC, submitted written comments on the draft First Amendment. The principal areas of comment and negotiation included the following:

(i) 180-Day Replacement Period Mechanics. WCA sought clarification and additional specificity regarding the mechanics of the 180-day Replacement Period triggered by the loss of one Successor Key Person, including the process for identifying and proposing a replacement, the voting threshold applicable to the replacement, and the consequences of a failure to replace within the 180-day period. C&H responded with proposed language establishing a structured replacement process, including a requirement that the General Partner submit a replacement proposal to the IAC within sixty (60) days, followed by a full LP consent solicitation within the remaining period.

(v) GP Fiduciary Obligations During Future Key Person Events. WCA requested the inclusion of an express statement in the First Amendment confirming the GP's ongoing fiduciary obligations to the limited partners during any future Key Person Event. C&H agreed to the inclusion of a confirmatory provision, noting that such obligations already existed under Delaware law and the A&R LPA but acknowledging that an express restatement would provide additional comfort to the LP base.

Thirty-eight (38) of the Fund's forty-seven (47) limited partners delivered executed written consents to C&H, representing aggregate LP capital commitments of $2,412.8 million.
