**[IX. Material Impediment Event, Dormancy, and Wind-Down Provisions]{.underline}**

**[A. Material Impediment Event (§7.04 of LP Agreement)]{.underline}**

The LP Agreement includes provisions addressing the possibility that the Cascadia acquisition may encounter material obstacles or impediments that prevent or delay the closing of the transaction. Pursuant to Section 7.04 of the LP Agreement, the General Partner may declare a \"Material Impediment Event\" and suspend capital calls and investment activity upon its determination that either:

> \(a\) a condition precedent to the closing of the Cascadia acquisition has failed or is reasonably expected to fail and is not reasonably likely to be cured or satisfied within ninety (90) days after such failure or expected failure; or
>
> \(b\) a Material Adverse Effect (as defined in the Equity Purchase Agreement governing the Cascadia acquisition) has occurred or is reasonably expected to occur with respect to Cascadia or its business, properties, or financial condition.

The Material Impediment Event provisions are designed to provide a structured framework for addressing significant obstacles to the Cascadia acquisition, including regulatory delays, financing disruptions, adverse changes in the target\'s business, and other events that could prevent or materially delay the closing of the transaction.

Upon the declaration of a Material Impediment Event, the General Partner is required to promptly notify the Limited Partner in writing. The notice must specify the basis for the General Partner\'s determination, including a reasonably detailed description of the relevant facts and circumstances, and must describe the actions that the General Partner intends to take in response to the Material Impediment Event.

**[B. Capital Call Suspension During Dormancy]{.underline}**

During the pendency of a Material Impediment Event, no further capital calls may be issued by the General Partner. The Limited Partner\'s unfunded capital commitment remains in place during the dormancy period but is not callable by the General Partner until such time as the General Partner determines that the Material Impediment Event has been resolved or the Limited Partner elects to wind down the Partnership in accordance with Section 7.04(c) of the LP Agreement.

Vehicle operating expenses incurred during the dormancy period are payable from the working-capital reserve established at first close or from previously called capital held by the Partnership. Based on preliminary estimates, annualized dormancy operating expenses are expected to be approximately One Hundred Eighty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$185,000), covering the following categories of expenses:

> • Fund administration services provided by Kendrick Thorne & Associates LLP
>
> • Registered agent fees payable to Cascade Systems
>
> • Delaware franchise tax
>
> • Annual audit costs
>
> • Schedule K-1 preparation and tax compliance costs
>
> • Miscellaneous administrative expenses

The Limited Partner\'s unfunded capital commitment is not at risk during the dormancy period, and the General Partner may not issue capital calls during dormancy except with the Limited Partner\'s prior written consent.

**[C. GP Quarterly Reporting During Dormancy]{.underline}**

During any period of dormancy, the General Partner is required to deliver quarterly status reports to the Limited Partner containing the following information:

> \(a\) the current status of the Material Impediment Event and any developments since the prior report, including a description of any actions taken by the General Partner to resolve or mitigate the impediment;
>
> \(b\) the status of any regulatory approvals required for the Cascadia acquisition and any communications with relevant regulatory authorities;
>
> \(c\) the status of any financing commitments for the acquisition, including any changes to the terms, availability, or conditionality of the financing;
>
> \(d\) the Partnership\'s financial position, including cash on hand, expenses incurred since the prior report, and remaining working-capital reserves available to fund dormancy operating expenses; and
>
> \(e\) the General Partner\'s assessment of the prospects for reactivation of the Vehicle and the closing of the Cascadia acquisition, or, if reactivation is unlikely, the General Partner\'s recommendation regarding the wind-down of the Partnership.

These quarterly dormancy reports are in addition to the standard quarterly reports required under the LP Agreement and are intended to provide Ironside with specific, detailed, and timely information regarding the status of the dormancy and the prospects for the Cascadia acquisition.

**[D. Wind-Down Election Right (§7.04(c))]{.underline}**

If the dormancy period exceeds eighteen (18) months from the date of the capital-call suspension notice, the Limited Partner has the right to elect the wind-down of the Partnership by delivering written notice of such election to the General Partner. This wind-down election right is one of the most important protective provisions negotiated on Ironside\'s behalf and provides Ironside with a clear exit mechanism in the event that the Cascadia acquisition cannot be completed within a reasonable timeframe.

Upon the Limited Partner\'s election to wind down the Partnership, the following steps are required:

> \(a\) The General Partner must take all steps necessary and appropriate to wind down the Partnership\'s affairs in an orderly manner, including the settlement of outstanding liabilities and obligations, the termination of service provider engagements, and the disposition or return of any assets held by the Partnership.
>
> \(b\) All uncommitted capital is released, and the Limited Partner\'s unfunded capital commitment is extinguished in full. The General Partner may not issue any further capital calls after the wind-down election.
>
> \(c\) Remaining assets of the Partnership, including any deposits, reserves, escrow amounts, and insurance interests, are distributed to the partners net of expenses and outstanding obligations, in accordance with the distribution waterfall set forth in Section 6.01 of the LP Agreement (see Section XI of this memorandum).
>
> \(d\) The Partnership files a Certificate of Cancellation with the Delaware Secretary of State in accordance with DRULPA Section 17-203, formally terminating the Partnership\'s legal existence.

The eighteen-month dormancy period is measured from the date of the General Partner\'s notice of capital-call suspension, not from the date of the declaration of the Material Impediment Event. This distinction is important because there may be a period between the declaration of the Material Impediment Event and the actual suspension of capital calls.

It is important to note that the wind-down election right is permissive, not mandatory. If the Limited Partner does not elect to wind down the Partnership after the eighteen-month period, the dormancy continues, subject to the General Partner\'s ongoing quarterly reporting obligations and other duties under the LP Agreement. The Limited Partner may exercise the wind-down election right at any time after the expiration of the eighteen-month period.

**[E. Reactivation]{.underline}**

If the Material Impediment Event is resolved prior to the Limited Partner\'s exercise of the wind-down election right, the General Partner may reactivate the Vehicle by delivering written notice of reactivation to the Limited Partner. Upon reactivation, the General Partner may recommence capital calls in accordance with Section 4.01 of the LP Agreement and proceed with the Cascadia acquisition.

Reactivation is subject to the Limited Partner\'s prior written consent if the underlying transaction terms have materially changed from those contemplated at the time of the Limited Partner\'s original commitment. Material changes include, without limitation, changes to the purchase price, enterprise value, equity contribution, financing terms, or governance arrangements of the Cascadia acquisition that would materially alter the risk/return profile of the investment. This consent requirement ensures that Ironside is not compelled to fund an investment on terms significantly different from those on which its commitment was originally made.

**[X. Term and Dissolution]{.underline}**

**[A. Term]{.underline}**

The term of the Partnership extends until the earliest to occur of any of the following events:

> \(a\) the completion of the Cascadia acquisition and the subsequent realization (through disposition, liquidation, or other exit) or abandonment of the investment;
>
> \(b\) an LP-elected wind-down following an extended dormancy period, as described in Section IX.D above;
>
> \(c\) a GP-initiated dissolution upon the General Partner\'s determination, in its reasonable judgment, that the Cascadia acquisition cannot be completed and that continuation of the Partnership is no longer in the best interests of the partners; and
>
> \(d\) the mutual written agreement of the General Partner and the Limited Partner to dissolve the Partnership.

The LP Agreement does not establish a fixed term (e.g., ten years) for the Partnership, which is typical for single-purpose co-investment vehicles. The term is instead tied to the life of the underlying investment, with appropriate dissolution triggers for scenarios in which the investment cannot be completed or is no longer viable.

**[B. Dissolution Events]{.underline}**

In addition to the events described above, the Partnership dissolves upon the occurrence of any of the following events:

> \(a\) the entry of a decree of judicial dissolution under DRULPA Section 17-802;
>
> \(b\) the removal of the General Partner without the appointment of a successor general partner, in accordance with the GP removal provisions described in Section VII above; and
>
> \(c\) the occurrence of any event that makes it unlawful for the Partnership to continue its business or affairs.

**[C. Winding Up]{.underline}**

Upon dissolution of the Partnership, the General Partner (or a liquidating trustee appointed by the Limited Partner if the General Partner has been removed) is responsible for winding up the Partnership\'s affairs. The winding-up process includes the liquidation of the Partnership\'s assets, the satisfaction of the Partnership\'s liabilities and obligations (including any indemnification obligations), and the distribution of remaining proceeds to the partners in accordance with the distribution waterfall set forth in Section 6.01 of the LP Agreement.

The winding-up process must be conducted in an orderly manner, with due regard for the interests of the partners and the Partnership\'s creditors. The General Partner (or liquidating trustee) must file a Certificate of Cancellation with the Delaware Secretary of State upon completion of the winding-up process, formally terminating the Partnership\'s legal existence.

**[XI. Distribution Waterfall]{.underline}**

Distributions of available cash or other property by the Partnership to its partners are made in the following order of priority, as set forth in Section 6.01 of the LP Agreement:

> **Step 1 --- Return of Contributed Capital.** First, to the Limited Partner and the General Partner, pro rata in proportion to their respective capital contributions, until each partner has received cumulative distributions equal to the aggregate amount of its capital contributions to the Partnership.
>
> **Step 2 --- Preferred Return.** Second, to the Limited Partner and the General Partner, pro rata in proportion to their respective capital contributions, until each partner has received cumulative distributions (including amounts distributed in Step 1) sufficient to provide an 8% per annum preferred return (compounded quarterly) on its contributed capital from the date each capital contribution was made through the date of distribution.
>
> **Step 3 --- GP Catch-Up / Carried Interest.** Third, 10% to the General Partner (as carried interest) and 90% to the Limited Partner and the General Partner pro rata in proportion to their respective capital contributions, until the General Partner has received 10% of all cumulative distributions made pursuant to Steps 1, 2, and 3 combined.
>
> **Step 4 --- Residual Distributions.** Fourth and thereafter, 10% to the General Partner (as carried interest) and 90% to the Limited Partner and the General Partner pro rata in proportion to their respective capital contributions.

The distribution waterfall is structured as a standard \"whole fund\" or \"European-style\" waterfall, in which the preferred return must be fully satisfied before any carried interest is payable to the General Partner. The 10% carried interest rate compares favorably to the 20% carried interest applicable in Fund IV\'s main limited partnership and reflects the negotiated economics of the co-investment arrangement.

**[XII. Transfer Restrictions]{.underline}**

The LP Agreement imposes customary restrictions on the transfer of partnership interests. Neither the General Partner nor the Limited Partner may transfer, assign, pledge, or otherwise dispose of its interest in the Partnership without the prior written consent of the other partner, except as follows:

> \(a\) **Transfers by the LP.** The Limited Partner may transfer its interest in the Partnership to one or more affiliates of Ironside Capital Management LP without the prior consent of the General Partner, subject to customary conditions, including (i) compliance with applicable federal and state securities laws, (ii) delivery by the transferee of a joinder agreement pursuant to which the transferee agrees to be bound by the terms of the LP Agreement, and (iii) delivery of such opinions of counsel and other documentation as the General Partner may reasonably request.
>
> \(b\) **Transfers by the GP.** The General Partner may transfer its interest in the Partnership to one or more affiliates of Meridian Infrastructure GP IV LLC without the prior consent of the Limited Partner, subject to the condition that the General Partner (or an affiliate thereof) continues to serve as the general partner of the Partnership following such transfer.

These transfer restrictions are designed to preserve the integrity of the partnership structure and to ensure that neither party may unilaterally introduce a new partner or alter the governance dynamics of the Vehicle without the consent of the other party.

**[XIII. Tax and Regulatory Considerations (Summary)]{.underline}**

The following is a summary of the key tax and regulatory considerations applicable to the Partnership. This summary is provided for informational purposes only and does not constitute a comprehensive analysis of the tax or regulatory issues applicable to the Vehicle. Detailed analyses of these matters are set forth in the separate memoranda referenced below.

**Tax Classification.** The Partnership is classified as a partnership for federal income tax purposes. As a partnership, the Vehicle is not subject to entity-level federal income tax. Instead, items of income, gain, loss, deduction, and credit flow through to the partners and are reported on their respective federal, state, and local income tax returns. This flow-through treatment is the standard and expected treatment for a Delaware limited partnership used as a co-investment vehicle.

**Schedule K-1 Preparation.** Schedule K-1 (Partner\'s Share of Income, Deductions, Credits, etc.) will be prepared and distributed to the partners annually by Kendrick Thorne & Associates LLP, the Partnership\'s fund administrator and tax preparer.

**Tax Structuring Analysis.** A detailed tax structuring analysis has been prepared separately by Sylvia Hartwell, Tax Partner at Calderwood & Harkness LLP, and is set forth in a memorandum dated July 20, 2022. The tax structuring memorandum addresses, among other things, the tax treatment of the carried interest under Section 1061 of the Internal Revenue Code, the allocation of income and loss items among the partners, and the state and local tax implications of the Partnership\'s investment in Cascadia.

**ERISA and Benefit Plan Investor Analysis.** A separate analysis has been prepared to confirm that the Vehicle is not subject to the plan-asset rules under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974 (\"ERISA\") and the regulations promulgated thereunder by the U.S. Department of Labor. The ERISA analysis is set forth in a memorandum dated July 27, 2022, and concludes that the Vehicle does not hold \"plan assets\" and is not subject to the fiduciary requirements and prohibited transaction rules of ERISA.

**Delaware Franchise Tax and Annual Report Filings.** The Partnership is required to file annual reports and pay the annual franchise tax imposed by the State of Delaware on limited partnerships. The annual franchise tax for Delaware limited partnerships is currently \$300. The Partnership\'s registered agent, Cascade Systems, will coordinate the filing of annual reports and the payment of franchise taxes.

**[3. Summary of Workstreams Completed]{.underline}**

**3.1 Workstream I --- Entity Restructuring**

**3.1.1 Formation of Holding Company Structure.** The centerpiece of the restructuring was the formation of a new two-tier holding company structure to replace the prior arrangement under which five individual principals held direct membership interests in both the GP and ManCo. Under the pre-restructuring arrangement, each of the five principals (Aldridge, Narayanan, Kellner, Trask, and Hsiao) held direct ownership percentages in both ManCo and the GP. This structure presented several challenges: (i) the departure of any principal required direct amendments to the governing documents of both ManCo and the GP, together with the re-execution of multiple ancillary agreements; (ii) the admission of new principals similarly required direct amendments at both the ManCo and GP levels; (iii) the platform lacked a centralized governance structure capable of facilitating efficient decision-making and succession planning; and (iv) the direct ownership structure created inefficiencies in connection with tax reporting, capital account administration, and allocation mechanics.

To address these challenges, Calderwood & Harkness designed and implemented a holding company structure consisting of two newly formed Delaware limited liability companies:

**Ardent Capital Holdings LLC (\"HoldCo\")** was formed as a new Delaware LLC on March 1, 2024, pursuant to a Certificate of Formation filed with the Delaware Secretary of State, Delaware File No. 7948231. The authorized person for the filing was Marcus Aldridge. The registered agent is Prestige Registered Agents LLC, located at 850 New Burton Road, Suite 201, Dover, Delaware 19904. HoldCo\'s EIN is 93-1847225. HoldCo serves as the parent holding company of both ManCo (as its direct sole member) and GP Intermediate (as its direct sole member). The five continuing principals hold their economic and governance interests in HoldCo, which centralizes ownership, governance, and economics at a single entity level.

**Ardent GP Intermediate LLC (\"GP Intermediate\")** was formed as a new Delaware LLC on March 1, 2024, pursuant to a Certificate of Formation filed with the Delaware Secretary of State, Delaware File No. 7948237. The authorized person for the filing was Marcus Aldridge. The registered agent is Prestige Registered Agents LLC at the same address. GP Intermediate\'s EIN is 93-1847231. GP Intermediate functions as an intermediate single-member entity between HoldCo and the GP. Its inclusion in the structure serves to provide an additional layer of liability separation between the holding company and the general partner entity, to facilitate future structural flexibility (including the potential admission of additional funds or co-investment vehicles at the GP level), and to preserve certain tax planning optionality identified by Sylvia Hartwell in the tax structuring memorandum.

Under the new structure, the organizational hierarchy is as follows:

> • The five continuing principals (Aldridge, Narayanan, Hsiao, Marchetti, and Okonkwo) hold membership interests in HoldCo.
>
> • HoldCo is the sole member of ManCo (directly).
>
> • HoldCo is the sole member of GP Intermediate.
>
> • GP Intermediate is the sole member of the GP.
>
> • The GP is the sole general partner of the Fund.

This structure permits future changes in principal-level ownership, economics, and governance to be accomplished through amendments to the HoldCo LLC Agreement alone, without the need to amend the governing documents of ManCo, the GP, or the Fund (except in circumstances requiring LP notification or consent under the LPA).

**3.1.2 Governing Documents Prepared and Executed.** The following governing documents were prepared, negotiated, and executed in connection with the entity restructuring workstream. All documents were executed as of February 28, 2024, with the new entity formations completed on March 1, 2024:

**[4. Tax Analysis Summary]{.underline}**

The tax aspects of the restructuring were addressed by Sylvia Hartwell (Specialist Partner, Tax), with analytical support from Stephen Adler.

A comprehensive **tax structuring memorandum** was delivered to the Client on November 22, 2023. The memorandum analyzed the federal income tax consequences of the proposed restructuring transactions and recommended a structural approach designed to achieve the most tax-efficient outcome for the principals. The key elements of the tax analysis are summarized below:

**HoldCo Formation --- IRC Section 721 Treatment.** The formation of HoldCo was structured as a tax-free contribution of the principals\' membership interests in the GP and ManCo to HoldCo in exchange for membership interests in HoldCo, qualifying for non-recognition treatment under Internal Revenue Code Section 721. Under Section 721, no gain or loss is recognized by the contributing partners or by HoldCo upon the contribution of property (including partnership interests) to a partnership in exchange for an interest in that partnership. This treatment was conditioned on proper documentation and compliance with the requirements of Section 721 and the applicable Treasury Regulations. The tax memorandum concluded that, if properly structured in accordance with the recommended approach, no taxable event would occur at the HoldCo formation level.

**Section 704(b)/704(c) Allocation Analysis.** Stephen Adler, under the supervision of Sylvia Hartwell, prepared a detailed **Section 704(b)/704(c) Allocation Analysis Memorandum** addressing the book-tax disparities arising from the carry reallocation, the treatment of the departing principals\' interests, and the methodology selection for the HoldCo operating agreement\'s allocation provisions. The analysis examined the following issues:

> • **Book-Tax Disparities from Carry Reallocation:** The reallocation of carried interest percentages creates book-tax disparities to the extent that the contributed interests have built-in gain or loss at the time of contribution to HoldCo. The memorandum analyzed the magnitude of these disparities based on the September 30, 2023 valuation data.
>
> • **Treatment of Departing Interests:** The memorandum addressed the tax treatment of the departing principals\' retained carry interests, concluding that such interests retain their character as partnership interests (i.e., as interests in the GP, which in turn holds an interest in the Fund) and are not recharacterized as a result of the restructuring.
>
> • **Methodology Selection:** The memorandum analyzed the relative merits of the traditional method and the remedial allocation method under Treasury Regulations Section 1.704-3 for addressing Section 704(c) allocations within HoldCo. After analysis of the specific facts and circumstances, the memorandum recommended the use of the remedial allocation method as the most appropriate approach for the HoldCo operating agreement, given the complexity of the contributing interests and the desire to achieve precise matching of tax items to economic entitlements.

**Key Tax Conclusions.** The principal tax conclusions of the engagement were as follows:

> 1\. No taxable event at the HoldCo formation level if the contribution is properly structured under IRC Section 721, with appropriate documentation of the contributing partners\' bases in their contributed interests and compliance with the applicable anti-abuse provisions.
>
> 2\. Joanna Trask\'s separation payment of \$1,250,000 is treated as ordinary income to Trask, subject to applicable withholding and reporting requirements. The payment is deductible by ManCo as a business expense in the tax year paid, subject to any applicable limitations.
>
> 3\. Carried interest retained by the departing principals (Kellner: \$13,140,000; Trask: \$6,307,200) retains its character as a partnership interest, and distributions on such retained carry will be taxed to the departing principals in accordance with the character of the underlying Fund income (i.e., capital gains or ordinary income, as applicable) and the provisions of IRC Section 1061 (applicable to carried interests held for less than three years).

All tax conclusions were discussed with the Client and coordinated with Heathrow Whitman & Co. for purposes of ongoing tax compliance and reporting.

**[I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"C&H\" or the \"Firm\") was engaged on June 11, 2024 by Driftwood Capital Management LLC (\"DCM\"), in its capacity as General Partner of Driftwood Absolute Return Fund Ltd. (\"DARF\" or the \"Fund\"), to advise on the legal implications of, and governance response to, a key-person event triggered by the sudden medical incapacitation of Marcus J. Whitmore, the Fund\'s founder, Chief Investment Officer, and sole designated Key Person under Section 8.04 of the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership, dated as of March 15, 2017 (the \"A&R LPA\"). The engagement arose under circumstances requiring immediate attention: Whitmore suffered a severe hemorrhagic stroke on June 3, 2024, and the contractual Key Person Event was deemed triggered on June 10, 2024 upon expiration of the seven-consecutive-calendar-day threshold set forth in Section 8.04(b) of the A&R LPA, thereby suspending the Fund\'s Investment Period and initiating a 90-calendar-day Cure Period expiring September 8, 2024.

The scope of the engagement, as set forth in the engagement letter dated June 11, 2024, encompassed the following principal workstreams: (i) comprehensive analysis of Section 8.04 key-person clause mechanics and the contractual consequences flowing from the triggering event; (ii) preparation and review of the limited partner notification required under Section 8.04(c); (iii) development and recommendation of a successor governance framework, including the designation of successor Key Persons and the establishment of an Investment Committee; (iv) drafting and negotiation of the First Amendment to the A&R LPA (the \"First Amendment\") to implement the successor governance framework; and (v) solicitation and tabulation of limited partner consents as required under the A&R LPA for approval of the successor Key Persons and the related amendments.

All engagement objectives were achieved within the contractual Cure Period and in compliance with all applicable provisions of the A&R LPA, Delaware law, and Cayman Islands regulatory requirements. Thirty-eight (38) of the Fund\'s forty-seven (47) limited partners delivered written consents representing \$2,412.8 million of LP capital commitments, or approximately 86.2% of voting LP commitments --- well in excess of the 66⅔% supermajority threshold required under Section 8.04(c). The First Amendment to the A&R LPA became effective on August 26, 2024, designating Elaine R. Sato and Jonathan K. Huang as joint Successor Key Persons, establishing a three-member Investment Committee, transitioning Marcus J. Whitmore to a Senior Advisor role without governance authority, and implementing a revised carried interest allocation among the principals of DCM. The Cure Period deadline of September 8, 2024 was thereby mooted by the successful completion of the successor governance process thirteen (13) calendar days in advance.

The engagement is closed as of September 2, 2024. The matter status is: **closed_completed**. No outstanding legal issues, open work items, or continuing obligations of the Firm remain as of the date of this memorandum.

**[IV. BACKGROUND: THE KEY-PERSON EVENT]{.underline}**

**A. Marcus J. Whitmore --- Profile**

Marcus J. Whitmore is the founder, Chief Investment Officer, and controlling Managing Member (90% membership interest) of Driftwood Capital Management LLC. Whitmore established DCM and the Fund in 2017 following a distinguished career spanning twenty-eight (28) years in multi-strategy institutional investing. Prior to founding DCM, Whitmore served as Managing Director and Head of Multi-Strategy Investing at Veltrano Asset Partners LLC from 2004 to 2016, where he oversaw a multi-billion-dollar allocation across equity long/short, event-driven, and credit strategies within the financial services sector. Before joining Veltrano, Whitmore served as a Portfolio Manager at Fieldstone Capital Advisors LP from 1996 to 2004, where he managed equity long/short portfolios focused on the banking and specialty finance sectors.

Whitmore was the sole designated \"Key Person\" under Section 8.04(a) of the A&R LPA. His designation as the sole Key Person reflected his central role in the Fund\'s investment process, including his direct management of the largest strategy books, his sole authority over portfolio construction and risk limits at the fund level, and his personal relationships with many of the Fund\'s largest institutional investors. Whitmore\'s capital commitment to the Fund was \$57.4 million, representing 2.0% of the Fund\'s assets under management as of May 31, 2024. His carried interest entitlement, prior to the amendment described herein, was 18% of the General Partner\'s 20% incentive allocation --- equivalent to 3.6% of the Fund\'s net new profits above the high-water mark.

**B. Incapacitation Event**

On June 3, 2024, Marcus J. Whitmore suffered a severe hemorrhagic stroke at his residence in New York City. Whitmore was transported to Lenox Hill Medical Center in New York, where he was admitted for emergency treatment and subsequently commenced an intensive neurorehabilitation program. According to information conveyed to DCM by Whitmore\'s immediate family and treating physicians, the attending neurological team projected a minimum recovery period of twelve (12) to eighteen (18) months, with an uncertain prognosis regarding Whitmore\'s ability to return to full-time professional activity. As of the date of this memorandum, Whitmore remains in a rehabilitation setting and has not resumed any professional duties with respect to DCM or the Fund.

The severity and sudden onset of Whitmore\'s medical condition meant that no advance notice was given to DCM, the limited partners, or any service provider prior to the incapacitation. DCM\'s Deputy CIO, Elaine R. Sato, assumed day-to-day operational and investment management responsibilities for the Fund on an interim basis effective June 3, 2024, subject to the contractual constraints described below.

**C. Key-Person Event Trigger Analysis**

Section 8.04(b) of the A&R LPA provides, in relevant part, as follows:

> A \"Key Person Event\" shall be deemed to have occurred if a Key Person designated pursuant to Section 8.04(a) is \"unable to devote substantially all of his professional time and attention to the affairs of the Partnership for a period of seven (7) consecutive calendar days,\" absent the prior written notice of such Key Person delivered to the General Partner and each member of the Investor Advisory Committee setting forth the anticipated duration and reason for such absence.

No prior written notice was delivered by Whitmore, as his incapacitation was sudden and unexpected. The incapacitation commenced on June 3, 2024. The seven-consecutive-calendar-day period prescribed by Section 8.04(b) elapsed at 11:59 p.m. (Eastern Time) on June 9, 2024, and accordingly the Key Person Event was deemed triggered as of the close of business on June 10, 2024 (the first business day following the expiration of the seven-day period). The C&H engagement team confirmed this trigger date through a detailed analysis of the A&R LPA\'s definitions and day-count conventions, as set forth in the Key-Person Event Analysis Memorandum delivered to DCM on June 13, 2024.

**D. Contractual Consequences (Section 8.04(c))**

Upon the occurrence of the Key Person Event, Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA imposed the following immediate and automatic consequences:

> \(i\) **Suspension of the Investment Period.** The Fund\'s Investment Period was immediately suspended. During the suspension, DCM was prohibited from making any new investments on behalf of the Fund. For purposes of this provision, a \"new investment\" was defined as any acquisition of a position not held in the Fund\'s portfolio as of the date of the Key Person Event.
>
> \(ii\) **Follow-On Investment Cap.** Follow-on investments in existing portfolio positions were permitted, but were capped at an aggregate of \$28.7 million (1.0% of AUM as of the most recent month-end preceding the Key Person Event, calculated as 1.0% of \$2.87 billion).
>
> \(iii\) **LP Notification Requirement.** The General Partner was required to notify all limited partners of the Fund in writing within five (5) business days of the occurrence of the Key Person Event. Given the Key Person Event trigger date of June 10, 2024 (a Monday), the five-business-day notification deadline fell on June 17, 2024 (the following Monday).
>
> \(iv\) **Commencement of the 90-Day Cure Period.** A Cure Period of ninety (90) calendar days commenced on June 10, 2024, expiring on September 8, 2024. During the Cure Period, the General Partner was afforded the opportunity to propose one or more Successor Key Persons, subject to approval by limited partners holding not less than 66⅔% of aggregate LP capital commitments (excluding the GP co-investment).
>
> \(v\) **Failure to Cure.** If no Successor Key Person was approved by the requisite supermajority of limited partners within the Cure Period, the A&R LPA provided that limited partners holding a majority-in-interest could elect either (a) to extend the Cure Period by up to ninety (90) additional calendar days, or (b) to commence an orderly wind-down of the Fund.

**E. LP Consent Voting Mechanics**

The approval threshold for designation of Successor Key Persons under Section 8.04(c) required the affirmative written consent of limited partners holding not less than 66⅔% of aggregate LP capital commitments, with the GP co-investment excluded from the denominator. The applicable calculations were as follows:

> • Total Fund AUM (May 31, 2024): \$2,870,000,000
>
> • Less: Marcus J. Whitmore GP co-investment: (\$57,400,000)
>
> • Less: Elaine R. Sato co-investment (as Managing Member of GP entity): (\$14,350,000)
>
> • Voting LP Capital Commitments: \$2,798,250,000
>
> • Required Consent Threshold (66⅔%): \$1,865,500,000

The foregoing calculation was confirmed in the Key-Person Event Analysis Memorandum and was consistent with the methodology specified in Section 14.01 of the A&R LPA for the computation of LP voting percentages.

**B. Revised Key Person Clause (Amended Section 8.04)**

The First Amendment revises Section 8.04 of the A&R LPA as follows:

> \(b\) **Loss of One Successor Key Person.** The loss of one Successor Key Person (whether by death, disability, resignation, termination, or other departure) triggers a 180-day Replacement Period. During the Replacement Period, the remaining Successor Key Person and the Investment Committee may continue to manage the Fund\'s investment activities without automatic suspension of the Investment Period. The General Partner must submit a replacement proposal to the IAC within sixty (60) days and conduct a full LP consent solicitation for the proposed replacement within the Replacement Period. 4\. **IRC § 367 Inapplicability to Partnership-to-Partnership Transfers** --- A memorandum analyzing the statutory text and legislative history of IRC § 367 and supporting the position that § 367 does not apply to transfers by a foreign partnership to a domestic partnership because the provision, by its terms, applies only to transfers to or from a \"foreign corporation.\"

5\. **IRC § 731(a) Distribution Analysis (Step 5)** --- A memorandum analyzing the application of IRC § 731(a) to the dissolution distributions by the four legacy offshore vehicles of their respective Master Fund LP interests to the existing limited partners, including analysis of the conditions for nonrecognition and the basis consequences under IRC § 732.

6\. **IRC § 731(c) Marketable Securities Exception Analysis** --- A memorandum specifically addressing whether the Master Fund LP limited partnership interests distributed in Step 5 constitute \"marketable securities\" as defined in IRC § 731(c)(2), and the consequences under IRC § 731(c)(1) if they were so classified.

7\. **IRC § 752 Liability Shifting Analysis** --- A comprehensive memorandum modeling the partner-level shares of the \$1.34 billion in aggregate liabilities being assumed by the Consolidated Master Fund LP, both before and after the reorganization. This analysis will address the netting rules under Treasury Regulation § 1.752-1(f), the tiered partnership rules applicable to the feeder-master fund structure, and the potential for deemed contributions or deemed distributions under IRC § 752(a) and (b) arising from shifts in partnership liabilities, including whether any such deemed distribution could trigger gain recognition under IRC § 731.

8\. **IRC § 704(c) Built-In Gain Carryover Analysis** --- A memorandum addressing the treatment of the \$1.72 billion in aggregate built-in gain upon contribution to the Consolidated Master Fund LP, including the carryover of built-in gain/loss accounts under IRC § 704(c)(1)(A) and the applicable Treasury Regulations.

9\. **IRC § 704(c) Remedial Allocation Method Election Continuation** --- A memorandum analyzing whether the remedial allocation method under Treasury Regulation § 1.704-3(d), previously elected by the contributing fund vehicles with respect to certain portfolio company interests, may continue to be applied by the Consolidated Master Fund LP following the contribution.

10\. **IRC § 1446 Withholding Analysis** --- A memorandum analyzing whether the contributions in Steps 2--4 or the distributions in Step 5 give rise to withholding obligations under IRC § 1446 and Treasury Regulations §§ 1.1446-1 through 1.1446-6, which impose withholding on effectively connected taxable income allocable to foreign partners of a partnership engaged in a U.S. trade or business.

11\. **FIRPTA / IRC § 897 Analysis** --- A memorandum analyzing whether any of the portfolio company interests being transferred constitute \"United States real property interests\" (\"USRPIs\") within the meaning of IRC § 897(c)(1), with particular attention to whether the data center facilities and fiber-optic network assets held by certain portfolio companies (including NovaBright Data Systems Inc. and Thorngate Fiber Networks LP) are treated as U.S. real property for purposes of the Foreign Investment in Real Property Tax Act (\"FIRPTA\").

12\. **Entity Classification Analysis Under Treas. Reg. § 301.7701-3** --- A memorandum confirming the entity classification of each new entity and each existing entity involved in the reorganization under the check-the-box regulations, including analysis of the default classification rules, the effectiveness of filed Form 8832 elections, and any implications of changes in entity membership.

13\. **Anti-Abuse Considerations** --- A memorandum addressing potential anti-abuse doctrines that the IRS might raise in connection with the reorganization, including the substance-over-form doctrine, the step transaction doctrine, and the partnership anti-abuse rule under Treasury Regulation § 1.701-2. This memorandum will analyze why, under the facts and circumstances, none of these doctrines should prevent the application of the intended tax treatment.

The **target completion date for the initial master tax analysis memorandum** is **June 16, 2025**. Completion dates for the individual topic-specific memoranda will follow on a rolling basis thereafter, with all memoranda completed in advance of the Version 1.0 draft of the PLR request.

**[B. Private Letter Ruling Request]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness will draft and iteratively revise the PLR request letter to be submitted to the IRS on behalf of Solara Digital Infrastructure LP and its affiliated fund entities. The PLR request will be addressed to the IRS, Office of the Associate Chief Counsel (International), CC:INTL, with secondary subject-matter jurisdiction in the Office of the Associate Chief Counsel (Passthroughs and Special Industries), CC:PSI. The submission address is:

> Internal Revenue Service
>
> Attn: CC:INTL
>
> 1111 Constitution Avenue NW Washington, DC 20224

The PLR request will seek the following **eight specific rulings** from the IRS:

**Ruling 1 (IRC § 721).** The contributions by the Legacy Offshore Vehicles of their portfolio company interests to the Consolidated Master Fund LP in Steps 2, 3, and 4 of the proposed reorganization constitute tax-free contributions under IRC § 721(a), and no gain or loss is recognized by any contributing partnership or by the Consolidated Master Fund LP upon such contributions.

**Ruling 2 (IRC § 721(b)).** The Consolidated Master Fund LP does not constitute an \"investment company\" within the meaning of IRC § 721(b) and Treasury Regulation § 1.351-1(c)(1)(ii), because the portfolio of assets contributed to and held by the Consolidated Master Fund LP consists of interests in operating companies engaged in the digital infrastructure and enterprise SaaS sectors, rather than \"stocks, securities, or other investment assets\" within the meaning of the applicable regulations.

**Ruling 3 (IRC § 367 Inapplicability).** IRC § 367 does not apply to the contributions described in Steps 2, 3, and 4 because IRC § 367(a) and (b), by their terms, apply only to transfers of property to or from a \"foreign corporation\" within the meaning of IRC § 7701(a)(5), and the Consolidated Master Fund LP is classified as a partnership --- not a corporation --- for U.S. federal income tax purposes under Treasury Regulation § 301.7701-3.

**Ruling 4 (IRC § 731).** The distributions by the Legacy Offshore Vehicles of their respective limited partnership interests in the Consolidated Master Fund LP to the existing limited partners in Step 5 of the proposed reorganization constitute tax-free distributions under IRC § 731(a), and IRC § 731(c) does not apply because the distributed Master Fund LP interests do not constitute \"marketable securities\" as defined in IRC § 731(c)(2).

**Ruling 5 (IRC § 752).** The shifts in partner-level shares of partnership liabilities arising from the reorganization do not result in deemed contributions or deemed distributions that would trigger gain recognition under IRC § 731, taking into account the netting rules under Treasury Regulation § 1.752-1(f) and the tiered partnership rules applicable to the post-reorganization feeder-master fund structure.

**Ruling 6 (IRC § 704(c)).** The built-in gain and built-in loss accounts attributable to the contributed portfolio company interests carry over from the Legacy Offshore Vehicles to the Consolidated Master Fund LP, and the remedial allocation method under Treasury Regulation § 1.704-3(d), previously elected by the contributing vehicles, may continue to be applied by the Consolidated Master Fund LP with respect to such interests.

**Ruling 7 (IRC § 1446).** No withholding is required under IRC § 1446 and Treasury Regulations §§ 1.1446-1 through 1.1446-6 in connection with the contributions in Steps 2--4 or the distributions in Step 5, because neither the contributions nor the distributions constitute allocations of effectively connected taxable income that would trigger a withholding obligation.

**Ruling 8 (Entity Classification).** The Consolidated Master Fund LP, the International Feeder (Cayman) LP, and the Tax-Exempt Feeder (Cayman) LP are each properly classified as partnerships for U.S. federal income tax purposes under Treasury Regulation § 301.7701-3, and such classifications are effective as of the dates specified in their respective IRS Form 8832 elections.

**Anticipated Drafting Timeline:**

The PLR request will be developed through an iterative drafting and review process as follows:

  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Version**             **Description**                                                                                                           **Target Date**
  ----------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Version 1.0             Internal draft for Calderwood & Harkness partner review                                                                   July 1, 2025

  Version 2.0             Post-partner review draft, circulated to client (Stefan Dalmqvist and Priya Narasimhan) for review and comment            Following partner review; targeted for circulation within 5 business days of v1.0

  Version 3.0             Post-client comment draft, circulated to LPAC counsel (Diana Carruthers, Whitfield, Carruthers & Doyle LLP) for review    July 15, 2025

  Version 4.0             Final circulated draft, incorporating LPAC counsel comments, for internal sign-off by Leonard Cross and Sylvia Hartwell   Following LPAC review

  Execution Version       Final execution version for submission to the IRS                                                                         August 15, 2025
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Each iteration will be tracked using document comparison technology, and all prior versions will be maintained in the engagement file. All draft versions circulated externally will bear the legend \"PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL --- ATTORNEY-CLIENT COMMUNICATION --- DRAFT --- NOT FOR SUBMISSION.\"

**[C. PLR Exhibits]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness will prepare the following exhibits to accompany the PLR request upon submission to the IRS:

**Exhibit A: Organizational Charts (Pre-Reorganization).** Detailed organizational charts depicting the existing fund platform structure, showing each of the six existing fund vehicles, the two general partner entities, the portfolio companies held by each vehicle, and the categories of limited partners investing through each vehicle. The charts will include full legal entity names, jurisdictions of formation, EINs, and ownership percentages.

**Exhibit B: Organizational Charts (Post-Reorganization).** Detailed organizational charts depicting the resulting fund platform structure after completion of all five reorganization steps, showing the Consolidated Master Fund LP, the two Cayman feeder vehicles, the continuing Delaware main funds (Fund IV LP and Fund V LP), and the allocation of limited partners across the post-reorganization vehicles.

**Exhibit C: Step Transaction Diagrams.** A series of visual diagrams depicting each of the five reorganization steps in chronological sequence, with target dates, descriptions of the assets and interests being transferred, and references to the applicable IRC sections and Treasury Regulations governing the tax treatment of each step.

**Exhibit D: Schedule of Contributing Entities and Assets.** A comprehensive tabular schedule identifying each contributing entity (transferor), each portfolio company interest being contributed (including full legal name, entity type, and jurisdiction), the fair market value, adjusted tax basis, and built-in gain attributable to each portfolio company interest, and the percentage ownership held by each contributing entity.

**Exhibit E: Schedule of Liabilities and § 752 Analysis.** A detailed schedule setting forth the pre-reorganization and post-reorganization allocations of partnership liabilities among the partners of each fund vehicle and the Consolidated Master Fund LP, together with a quantitative analysis demonstrating the application of the netting rules under Treasury Regulation § 1.752-1(f) and the tiered partnership rules to the liability shifts arising from the reorganization.

**[D. IRS Procedural Documents]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness will prepare and file the following procedural documents and submissions in connection with the PLR process:

**IRS Form 2848 (Power of Attorney and Declaration of Representative).** Calderwood & Harkness will prepare and file IRS Form 2848 designating Leonard Cross and Sylvia Hartwell as the authorized representatives of Solara Digital Infrastructure LP (EIN 82-4917366), Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC (EIN 82-4917365), and all affiliated fund entities with respect to the PLR request and all related communications with the IRS.

**Penalties of Perjury Declaration.** Calderwood & Harkness will prepare the penalties of perjury declaration required under Rev. Proc. 2025-1 to accompany the PLR request, which must be signed by an authorized officer of the applicant. Viktor Raines, in his capacity as the managing member of Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC (the general partner of Solara Digital Infrastructure LP), will be requested to execute this declaration.

**IRS User Fee Payment Transmittal Letter.** Calderwood & Harkness will prepare the transmittal letter accompanying the IRS user fee payment of \$38,000, which is required under the fee schedule set forth in Rev. Proc. 2025-1 for PLR requests involving multiple entities with combined assets exceeding \$50 million. Calderwood & Harkness will coordinate with Solara\'s finance team on the wire transfer of the user fee to the IRS.

**Pre-Submission Conference Request Letter.** Calderwood & Harkness will prepare and submit a letter to IRS CC:INTL Branch 1 requesting a pre-submission conference with the IRS technical staff to discuss the proposed PLR request before formal submission. The requested date for the pre-submission conference is **July 22, 2025**. Pre-submission conferences are governed by Section 10.07 of Rev. Proc. 2025-1 and provide an opportunity to discuss the proposed transaction structure, the specific rulings to be requested, and any issues the IRS technical staff may wish to raise before the formal submission is prepared. Leonard Cross will attend the pre-submission conference on behalf of Calderwood & Harkness, and Sylvia Hartwell may also attend depending on scheduling.

**Post-Conference Summary Memorandum.** Following the pre-submission conference, Calderwood & Harkness will prepare a detailed internal memorandum summarizing the conference discussions, any substantive feedback or concerns raised by the IRS technical staff, any modifications to the PLR request suggested or required by the IRS, and any additional factual information or legal analysis requested. This memorandum will be circulated to Stefan Dalmqvist and Priya Narasimhan.

**Supplemental Submission Letters.** As needed during the post-submission review period, Calderwood & Harkness will prepare and submit supplemental letters to the IRS responding to any questions, requests for additional information, or proposed modifications raised by the IRS technical staff in the course of their review of the PLR request.

**PLR Submission Transmittal Letter.** Calderwood & Harkness will prepare the formal transmittal letter accompanying the PLR request and all supporting exhibits, declarations, powers of attorney, and user fee payment upon submission to the IRS. The target date for formal submission is **August 15, 2025**.

**[E. Entity Formation Support]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness will provide the following entity formation support services in connection with the establishment of the four new entities described in Step 1 of the reorganization:

> • **Review and Comment on Formation Documents.** Calderwood & Harkness will review and provide tax-related comments on the draft formation documents for each new entity, including the Certificate of Formation for Solara Consolidated Master Fund GP LLC (Delaware), the Certificate of Limited Partnership for Solara Consolidated Master Fund LP (Delaware), and the draft Limited Partnership Agreement for Solara Consolidated Master Fund LP. The review will focus on provisions with tax implications, including allocations, distributions, capital accounts, and partnership termination provisions. The preparation of the underlying formation documents is outside the scope of this engagement and is expected to be handled by Solara\'s corporate counsel.
>
> • **IRS Form 8832 Elections.** Calderwood & Harkness will prepare IRS Form 8832 (Entity Classification Election) for each of the three new partnership entities --- the Consolidated Master Fund LP, the International Feeder (Cayman) LP, and the Tax-Exempt Feeder (Cayman) LP --- electing classification as a partnership for U.S. federal income tax purposes under Treasury Regulation § 301.7701-3.
>
> • **Timing Memorandum.** Calderwood & Harkness will prepare a memorandum analyzing the optimal timing of the check-the-box elections, including coordination of the election effective dates with the target dates for each reorganization step and the application of the 75-day retroactivity rule under Treasury Regulation § 301.7701-3(c)(1)(iii).
>
> • **Instruction Letters to Foreign Counsel.** Calderwood & Harkness will prepare instruction letters to Meridian Offshore Legal (for Cayman Islands entity formation and subsequent dissolution of legacy Cayman vehicles) and to Veldhuis & Gérard S.à r.l. (for dissolution of the Luxembourg SCSps), specifying the formation parameters, timing requirements, and U.S. tax considerations that foreign counsel should take into account in preparing the foreign entity formation and dissolution documentation.

**[F. Lender Consent Support]{.underline}**

The proposed reorganization will affect the collateral and borrowing base structures underlying two existing subscription credit facilities maintained by the Solara fund vehicles. Calderwood & Harkness will provide the following support in connection with obtaining lender consents:

> • **Lender Consent Request Letters.** Calderwood & Harkness will prepare lender consent request letters addressed to:
>
> \(i\) **Ashford National Bank, N.A.** (Thomas Greenleaf, Managing Director, Fund Finance), the administrative agent under the \$1.1 billion Fund IV subscription credit facility; and
>
> \(ii\) **Ashford National Bank, N.A.** and **Sentinel Capital Markets LLC** (Laura Pak, Vice President), the co-administrative agents under the \$1.5 billion Fund V subscription credit facility.
>
> • **Consent and Amendment Agreements.** Calderwood & Harkness will draft the consent and amendment agreements for both credit facilities, addressing any required changes to the definitions of \"Eligible Investors,\" \"Borrowing Base,\" and \"Permitted Transfers,\" and any modifications to change-of-control, assignment, and event-of-default provisions necessitated by the reorganization.
>
> • **Analysis Memorandum.** Calderwood & Harkness will prepare an internal analysis memorandum identifying the credit facility provisions most likely implicated by the reorganization, including change-of-control provisions, borrowing base impact, assignment restrictions, and any requirements for pledge or collateral modification.

**[G. LP Communication and Consent Support]{.underline}**

The proposed reorganization requires formal limited partner consent under the applicable provisions of the Fund IV and Fund V limited partnership agreements. Calderwood & Harkness notes that preliminary consent of 78% in interest was obtained from the LP Advisory Committee (\"LPAC\") at the meeting held on April 22, 2025. Calderwood & Harkness will provide the following support to facilitate the formal LP consent process:

> • **LPAC Presentation Materials.** Calderwood & Harkness will prepare presentation materials for LPAC meetings summarizing the reorganization, the intended tax treatment of each step, the anticipated timeline, and the status of the PLR request.
>
> • **LP Consent Solicitation Letter.** Calderwood & Harkness will draft the LP consent solicitation letter to be distributed to all limited partners in the four legacy offshore vehicles, together with the form of LP consent to be executed and returned by each limited partner.
>
> • **LP Tax Impact Summary Letter.** Calderwood & Harkness will prepare a plain-language tax impact summary letter for distribution to limited partners, summarizing the anticipated U.S. federal income tax consequences of the reorganization for each category of investor: (i) U.S. taxable investors, (ii) U.S. tax-exempt investors, and (iii) non-U.S. investors. This letter will include appropriate caveats that each limited partner should consult its own tax advisors regarding its individual circumstances.
>
> • **LPA Amendments.** Calderwood & Harkness will draft the amendments to the Fund IV Limited Partnership Agreement and the Fund V Limited Partnership Agreement necessary to authorize the general partner to cause the fund vehicles to contribute their portfolio company assets to the Consolidated Master Fund LP.

**[H. Third-Party Coordination and Notifications]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness will prepare the following third-party notification and coordination documents:

> • **Insurance Broker Notification.** Calderwood & Harkness will prepare a notification letter to Hawkstone Specialty Insurance Co. (Neil Braddock, Senior Underwriter) regarding the endorsement or amendment of existing \$50 million directors\' and officers\' / errors and omissions liability insurance policies to cover the officers and directors of the newly formed entities.
>
> • **Fund Administrator Notification.** Calderwood & Harkness will prepare a notification letter to Clarendon Fund Services Ltd. (Rachel Okonkwo, Client Relationship Director) regarding the transition of NAV calculation and investor reporting responsibilities from the legacy offshore vehicle structure to the post-reorganization consolidated structure.
>
> • **Valuation Coordination.** Calderwood & Harkness will coordinate with Redstone Advisory Group LLC (Marco DeLuca, Managing Director, 750 Seventh Avenue, 21st Floor, New York, NY 10019) on the engagement for fair market value appraisals of all portfolio company interests being transferred in the reorganization. Calderwood & Harkness will prepare a valuation engagement cover memorandum specifying the tax-related requirements for the appraisals, including the applicable valuation date(s), the standard of value to be applied, and the IRS-required disclosures for appraisals submitted in connection with a PLR request.
>
> • **Accounting Coordination.** Calderwood & Harkness will coordinate with Caldwell Pierce & Co. LLP (Helen Okamoto, Partner, Financial Services Tax) on the collection and verification of historical financial data, prior-year tax returns (Forms 1065), and Schedules K-1 for all fund vehicles, which will be required as supporting documentation for the PLR exhibits and the IRC § 704(c) and § 752 analyses.

**[I. Internal Work Product and Administration]{.underline}**

In addition to the client-facing deliverables described above, Calderwood & Harkness will prepare and maintain the following internal work product and administrative materials throughout the engagement:

> • **Research Memorandum --- Analogous PLRs.** Calderwood & Harkness will prepare a research memorandum surveying previously issued private letter rulings involving partnership reorganizations, cross-border fund restructurings, and the specific IRC provisions at issue, identifying precedents that support the requested rulings and distinguishing any adverse rulings.
>
> • **Issue Tracking Lot the IRS will accept the PLR request for consideration under its published procedures. However, there can be no guarantee that the IRS will accept the PLR request, agree to rule on all of the requested issues, issue a favorable ruling on any or all of the eight specific rulings requested, or refrain from issuing an adverse ruling on any issue. The IRS retains broad discretion in the administration of the PLR process, including the discretion to decline to rule on particular issues, to raise issues not addressed in the PLR request, and to request additional information or analysis.

**[C. Timing Assumptions]{.underline}**

The engagement timeline is predicated on the following key dates and milestones. Each date assumes the timely provision of requested data by the client and its other advisors, timely review and feedback on draft deliverables, and the availability of IRS technical staff for the pre-submission conference on or about the requested date.

  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Milestone**                                                             **Target Date**
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------- -----------------------------------
  Initial tax analysis memorandum delivered to client                       June 16, 2025

  Draft PLR request (Version 1.0) to Calderwood & Harkness partner review   July 1, 2025

  Draft PLR request circulated to LPAC counsel                              July 15, 2025

  Pre-submission conference with IRS CC:INTL                                July 22, 2025

  PLR submission to IRS                                                     August 15, 2025

  Formation of new entities (Step 1)                                        September 15, 2025

  Step 2 --- Fund IV-A Cayman contribution                                  October 1, 2025

  Step 3 --- Fund IV-B Luxembourg contribution                              October 15, 2025

  Step 4 --- Fund V offshore contributions                                  November 1, 2025

  Step 5 --- Dissolution of legacy vehicles and LP migration                December 1, 2025
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Any delay in the provision of data, client feedback, or third-party coordination --- or any delay by the IRS in scheduling the pre-submission conference or processing the PLR request --- may require adjustment to the timeline. Calderwood & Harkness will promptly notify the client of any anticipated delays and will work collaboratively with the client to adjust the timeline as necessary.

**[D. EUR/USD Exchange Rate]{.underline}**

All EUR-denominated amounts referenced in this memorandum and in the PLR request are converted to U.S. dollars at an exchange rate of 1.08 EUR/USD (i.e., €1.00 = \$1.08). This rate is applied uniformly throughout the analysis for consistency. If a different exchange rate is determined to be more appropriate at the time of the PLR submission --- for example, based on the prevailing spot rate on the date of submission or the weighted average rate over a specified period --- the financial schedules in the PLR request and exhibits will be updated accordingly.

**[VIII. Coordination with Other Advisors]{.underline}**

The proposed reorganization involves multiple professional advisors in several jurisdictions. Calderwood & Harkness will serve as the central coordinator for the tax workstream and PLR submission, consolidating input from all advisors as needed. The following sections describe the other advisors involved and the scope of Calderwood & Harkness\'s coordination with each.

**[A. Legal Advisors]{.underline}**

> • **Meridian Offshore Legal** (Fiona McAllister, Partner) --- Cayman Islands counsel. Responsible for formation and dissolution of Cayman Islands entities, CIMA registration and deregistration, and compliance with Cayman economic substance requirements. Calderwood & Harkness will provide instruction letters regarding U.S. tax considerations relevant to the Cayman entity formation and dissolution process and will coordinate with Meridian on timing and sequencing.
>
> • **Veldhuis & Gérard S.à r.l.** (Marc Gérard, Managing Partner) --- Luxembourg counsel. Responsible for dissolution and liquidation of the Luxembourg SCSps, notification to the CSSF, Luxembourg tax clearance, and analysis under the Luxembourg law of July 12, 2013. Calderwood & Harkness will coordinate with Veldhuis & Gérard on the Luxembourg tax treatment of the asset transfers and any Luxembourg withholding tax or registration duty implications.
>
> • **Whitfield, Carruthers & Doyle LLP** (Diana Carruthers, Partner, Fund Formation & Tax) --- LPAC counsel. Diana Carruthers and her team represent the LP Advisory Committee and will review the PLR request for purposes of advising the LPAC on LP consent matters. Calderwood & Harkness will circulate the Version 3.0 draft of the PLR request to Ms. Carruthers and will incorporate LPAC counsel comments as appropriate, subject to the client\'s direction.
>
> • **Bramhall & Quelwick LLP** (Jason Tremaine, Partner, International Tax) --- Independent tax counsel to Nordhaven Sovereign Wealth Fund. Mr. Tremaine\'s team is evaluating the U.S. withholding tax and treaty implications of the reorganization from the perspective of Nordhaven. **3.1 Overview of the Transaction**

Solara is undertaking a cross-border reorganization of its fund platform (the \"Reorganization\"), involving the domestication and merger of several Cayman Islands and Luxembourg fund vehicles into a newly established Delaware-domiciled master fund structure. The Reorganization is designed to simplify the Client\'s fund architecture, reduce administrative and operational costs, enhance investor reporting, and achieve certain tax efficiencies in connection with the ongoing management and eventual disposition of portfolio company interests.

The Reorganization involves the following existing fund vehicles (collectively, the \"Legacy Fund Vehicles\"):

> \(i\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund IV LP** --- a Delaware limited partnership with approximately \$4.2 billion in committed capital (vintage 2021), approximately 72% deployed as of the date hereof;
>
> \(ii\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP** --- a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership with approximately \$1.85 billion in committed capital, operating as a parallel fund to Fund IV for U.S. tax-exempt and non-U.S. investors;
>
> \(iii\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund IV-B (Luxembourg) SCSp** --- a Luxembourg special limited partnership (*société en commandite spéciale*) with approximately €1.15 billion in committed capital (approximately \$1.24 billion at an assumed exchange rate of 1.08 EUR/USD), operating as a parallel fund to Fund IV for certain European institutional investors;
>
> \(iv\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund V LP** --- a Delaware limited partnership with approximately \$5.6 billion in committed capital (vintage 2023), approximately 38% deployed as of the date hereof;
>
> \(v\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund V-A (Cayman) LP** --- a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership with approximately \$2.45 billion in committed capital, operating as a parallel fund to Fund V for U.S. tax-exempt and non-U.S. investors; and
>
> \(vi\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund V-B (Luxembourg) SCSp** --- a Luxembourg special limited partnership (*société en commandite spéciale*) with approximately €1.38 billion in committed capital (approximately \$1.49 billion at an assumed exchange rate of 1.08 EUR/USD), operating as a parallel fund to Fund V for certain European institutional investors.

The Reorganization contemplates the formation of the following new entities (collectively, the \"New Fund Vehicles\"):

> \(i\) **Solara Consolidated Master Fund LP** --- a Delaware limited partnership to serve as the master fund in a restructured master-feeder architecture;
>
> \(ii\) **Solara Consolidated Master Fund GP LLC** --- a Delaware limited liability company to serve as the general partner of the Consolidated Master Fund;
>
> \(iii\) **Solara International Feeder (Cayman) LP** --- a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership to serve as the feeder vehicle for non-U.S. investors; and
>
> \(iv\) **Solara Tax-Exempt Feeder (Cayman) LP** --- a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership to serve as the feeder vehicle for U.S. tax-exempt investors.

The Reorganization involves a multi-step transaction that includes, among other things, asset contributions by the four offshore Legacy Fund Vehicles to the Consolidated Master Fund, the dissolution of the legacy offshore vehicles following such contributions, and the migration of existing limited partners into the appropriate new feeder structure. The target effective date for the completion of the Reorganization is December 1, 2025. The precise sequencing and mechanics of the multi-step transaction will be developed and refined in the course of the engagement, in consultation with the Client and its other advisors.

**Section 10.2 --- Tax Returns and Information**

\(a\) The General Partner shall cause the Partnership to prepare and timely file all required United States federal, state, local, and foreign tax returns, including IRS Form 1065 (U.S. Return of Partnership Income) and any applicable state or local partnership returns.

\(b\) The General Partner shall furnish to each Partner a Schedule K-1 (Form 1065) and any other required tax reporting information within ninety (90) days after the end of each Fiscal Year, or such earlier date as may be required by applicable law.

\(c\) Tax compliance services for the Partnership shall be provided by Caldwell Pierce & Co. LLP (Partner: Helen Okamoto), under the direction and supervision of the General Partner and the Head of Tax, Stefan Dalmqvist.

**Section 10.3 --- Tax Elections**

The General Partner shall have the sole authority to make any and all tax elections on behalf of the Partnership, including but not limited to:

\(a\) Entity classification elections under Treasury Regulations Section 301.7701-3 (IRS Form 8832);

\(b\) Elections under IRC Section 754 (optional adjustment to basis of partnership property);

\(c\) Elections regarding methods of accounting and accounting periods;

\(d\) The election to use the Remedial Allocation Method under Treasury Regulations Section 1.704-3(d) for all Section 704(c) Property (as further described in Section 5.4(c));

\(e\) Elections under IRC Section 168 (depreciation methods and recovery periods); and

\(f\) Any other elections permitted or required under the Code or the Regulations that the General Partner determines, in its sole discretion, to be in the best interests of the Partnership and the Partners.

**Section 10.4 --- FIRPTA Considerations**

\(a\) The General Partner shall monitor on an ongoing basis whether any of the Partnership\'s portfolio company interests constitute United States Real Property Interests (\"USRPIs\") within the meaning of IRC Section 897(c). This analysis is particularly relevant to the Partnership\'s investments in data center and fiber-optic network businesses, including NovaBright Data Systems Inc. and Thorngate Fiber Networks LP, which may hold substantial interests in real property located in the United States.

\(b\) If any Portfolio Company interest (or the Partnership itself) is determined to constitute a USRPI, the Partnership shall comply with all FIRPTA withholding and reporting requirements under IRC Section 897 and IRC Section 1445, including the filing of IRS Forms 8288 and 8288-A, as applicable.

\(c\) The FIRPTA analysis is of particular relevance to the non-U.S. investors investing through the International Feeder. The General Partner shall provide the International Feeder with such information as is necessary for the International Feeder to comply with its own FIRPTA reporting and withholding obligations with respect to its non-U.S. limited partners.

**Section 10.5 --- UBTI Considerations**

\(a\) The General Partner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to structure the Partnership\'s activities and investments in a manner that minimizes the generation of UBTI allocable to U.S. tax-exempt investors investing through the Tax-Exempt Feeder.

\(b\) The Tax-Exempt Feeder\'s structure, including the use of corporate subsidiary holding structures (Blocker corporations) interposed between the Tax-Exempt Feeder and certain Partnership investments, is designed to block UBTI from flowing through to U.S. tax-exempt investors. The General Partner shall coordinate with the Tax-Exempt Feeder\'s general partner to maintain the effectiveness of such UBTI blocker structures.

\(c\) Notwithstanding the foregoing, the General Partner does not guarantee that no UBTI will be generated by the Partnership or allocated to the Tax-Exempt Feeder or its underlying tax-exempt investors. Each U.S. tax-exempt investor should consult its own tax advisors regarding UBTI and related considerations.

**Section 10.6 --- Withholding Tax Compliance**

\(a\) The Partnership shall comply with all applicable withholding tax requirements under United States federal, state, and local law and foreign law, including but not limited to:

> \(i\) IRC Section 1446 (withholding on effectively connected taxable income allocable to foreign partners);
>
> \(ii\) FATCA (IRC Sections 1471 through 1474 and any applicable intergovernmental agreements) (requiring withholding on certain payments to foreign financial institutions and non-financial foreign entities that fail to comply with certain identification and reporting requirements);
>
> \(iii\) The Common Reporting Standard (\"CRS\") adopted pursuant to the OECD Standard for Automatic Exchange of Financial Account Information in Tax Matters; and
>
> \(iv\) Any other applicable withholding or reporting regime imposed by a foreign taxing jurisdiction.

\(b\) Each Partner shall provide the Partnership with a properly completed and executed IRS Form W-9 (for U.S. persons) or the applicable IRS Form W-8 (W-8BEN, W-8BEN-E, W-8IMY, or W-8ECI, as appropriate) (for non-U.S. persons) upon admission to the Partnership and upon request thereafter. Each Partner shall promptly notify the General Partner of any change in the information provided on such forms and shall provide updated forms as necessary.

**Section 10.7 --- Private Letter Ruling**

\(a\) The Partnership acknowledges that the Reorganization giving rise to its formation is the subject of a private letter ruling request (the \"**PLR Request**\") submitted to the Internal Revenue Service, Office of the Associate Chief Counsel (International) (CC:INTL), with secondary jurisdiction in the Office of the Associate Chief Counsel (Passthroughs & Special Industries) (CC:PSI), on or about August 15, 2025.

\(b\) The PLR Request seeks rulings from the IRS on, among other things:

> \(i\) the tax-free treatment of the contributions of portfolio company interests by the Legacy Offshore Vehicles to the Partnership under IRC Section 721(a);
>
> \(ii\) the inapplicability of IRC Section 721(b) (relating to contributions to investment companies) and IRC Section 367 (relating to transfers of property from the United States) to the contributions;
>
> \(iii\) the tax-free treatment of distributions of Partnership Interests to the underlying investors of the Legacy Offshore Vehicles upon the dissolution of the Legacy Offshore Vehicles in Step 5 of the Reorganization under IRC Section 731(a);
>
> \(iv\) the inapplicability of IRC Section 731(c) (relating to distributions of marketable securities) to such distributions;
>
> \(v\) the proper treatment of the assumption of liabilities by the Partnership under IRC Section 752, including the netting of deemed contributions and deemed distributions arising from shifts in partners\' shares of liabilities;
>
> \(vi\) the carryover of Section 704(c) accounts from the Legacy Offshore Vehicles to the Partnership and the proper application of the Remedial Allocation Method under Treasury Regulations Section 1.704-3(d);
>
> \(vii\) the absence of withholding tax obligations under IRC Section 1446 in connection with the contributions and distributions occurring as part of the Reorganization; and
>
> \(viii\) the classification of the Partnership, the International Feeder, and the Tax-Exempt Feeder as partnerships for United States federal income tax purposes.

\(c\) The terms and provisions of this Agreement are intended to be consistent with the representations, analysis, and legal arguments set forth in the PLR Request. In the event of any conflict between the terms of this Agreement and the representations made in the PLR Request, the General Partner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to reconcile such conflict in a manner consistent with the rulings sought in the PLR Request.

(a) Billing Rates
